title.zh: 卷四百九十二 列傳第二百五十一 外國八 吐蕃唃廝囉 董氊 阿里骨 瞎征 趙思忠
title.en: Volume 492 Biographies 251: Foreign States 8: Gusiluo of Tubo, Dongzhan, Aligu, Xiazheng, Zhao Sizhong
title.raw: 卷四百九十二 列傳第二百五十一 外國八 吐蕃唃廝囉 董氊 阿里骨 瞎征 趙思忠 Volume 492 Biographies 251: Foreign States 8: Gusiluo of Tubo, Dongzhan, Aligu, Xiazheng, Zhao Sizhong

sentences.zh: 吐蕃

translations.literal: Tubo.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo

sentences.zh: 〈（唃廝囉 董氈 阿裏骨 瞎征 趙思忠）〉

translations.literal: (Gusiluo, Dongzhan, Aligu, Xiazheng, Zhao Sizhong).
translations.idiomatic: (Gusiluo, Dongzhan, Aligu, Xiazheng, Zhao Sizhong)

sentences.zh: 〈（唃廝囉 董氈 阿裏骨 瞎征 趙思忠）〉

translations.literal: (Gusiluo, Dongzhan, Aligu, Xiazheng, Zhao Sizhong).
translations.idiomatic: (Gusiluo, Dongzhan, Aligu, Xiazheng, Zhao Sizhong)

sentences.zh: 吐蕃本漢西羌之地，其種落莫知所出。

translations.literal: Tubo was originally the land of the Western Qiang in Han times; the origin of its tribes is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo occupied what had been the Western Qiang lands in Han times, but the origins of its tribes remain unknown.

sentences.zh: 或云南涼禿髮利鹿孤之後，其子孫以禿髮為國號，語訛故謂之吐蕃。

translations.literal: Some say they were descendants of Tufa Lilugu of Southern Liang; his descendants took Tufa as the name of their state, and through corruption of speech they were called Tubo.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that they were descended from Tufa Lilugu of Southern Liang, whose line took Tufa as its dynastic name—a term that, through phonetic corruption, came to be pronounced Tubo.

sentences.zh: 唐貞觀後，常來朝貢。

translations.literal: After the Zhenguan era of Tang, they regularly came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhenguan reign of Tang, they regularly sent tribute missions to court.

sentences.zh: 至德後，因安、史之亂，遂陷河西、隴右之地。

translations.literal: After the Zhide era, because of the An Lushan and Shi Siming rebellion, they then seized the lands of Hexi and Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhide reign, the An-Shi Rebellion enabled them to overrun Hexi and Longyou.

sentences.zh: 大中三年，其國宰相論恐熱以秦、原、安樂及石門等七關來歸。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dazhong, their state's chancellor Lun Qinre came over with the seven passes of Qin, Yuan, Anle, and Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dazhong (849), the Tubo chancellor Lun Qinre submitted Qin, Yuan, Anle, Shimen, and four other frontier passes—seven in all.

sentences.zh: 四年，又克成、維、扶三州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, they also captured the three prefectures of Cheng, Wei, and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they also recovered the prefectures of Cheng, Wei, and Fu.

sentences.zh: 五年，其國沙州刺史張義潮以瓜、沙、伊、肅十一州之地來獻。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Zhang Yichao, prefect of Shazhou in their state, presented the lands of the eleven prefectures of Gua, Sha, Yi, and Su.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (851), Shazhou prefect Zhang Yichao offered up the territory of eleven prefectures—Gua, Sha, Yi, Su, and seven others.

sentences.zh: 唐末，瓜、沙之地復為所隔。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang, the lands of Gua and Sha were again cut off by them.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Tang, Gua and Sha were once again severed from the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 然而其國亦自衰弱，族種分散，大者數千家，小者百十家，無復統一矣。

translations.literal: Yet their state itself also weakened; clans and peoples scattered—the large numbering several thousand households, the small a hundred or ten—and there was no longer unity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Tubo itself had grown feeble: tribes splintered into groups of a few thousand households at most and as few as a hundred or ten, and no central authority remained.

sentences.zh: 自儀、渭、涇、原、環、慶及鎮戎、秦州暨於靈、夏皆有之，各有首領，內屬者謂之熟戶，餘謂之生戶。

translations.literal: From Yi, Wei, Jing, Yuan, Huan, Qing, and Zhenrong and Qinzhou down to Ling and Xia they were all present, each with its own leader; those who submitted inward were called subject households, the rest raw households.
translations.idiomatic: They were found from Yi, Wei, Jing, Yuan, Huan, and Qing through Zhenrong and Qinzhou to Lingzhou and Xiazhou, each band under its own chief; those who had submitted were called subject tribes, the rest raw tribes.

sentences.zh: 涼州雖為所隔，然其地自置牧守，或請命於中朝。

translations.literal: Although Liangzhou was cut off by them, that region itself appointed pastoral officials and prefects, or sought appointment from the central court.
translations.idiomatic: Though Liangzhou lay beyond imperial reach, the city still appointed its own local administrators and sometimes petitioned the central court for recognition.

sentences.zh: 天成中，權知西涼府留後孫超遣大將拓拔承誨來貢，明宗召見，承誨云：「涼州東距靈武千里，西北至甘州五百里。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era, Sun Chao, acting military governor of Western Liang, sent the great general Tuoba Chenghui to present tribute; Emperor Mingzong summoned and received him, and Chenghui said: "Liangzhou is a thousand li east from Lingwu and five hundred li northwest to Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng era (926–930), Sun Chao, acting prefect of Western Liang, sent his general Tuoba Chenghui to court with tribute. Emperor Mingzong received him, and Chenghui reported: "Liangzhou lies a thousand li east of Lingwu and five hundred li northwest of Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 舊有鄆人二千五百為戍兵，及黃巢之亂，遂為阻絕。

translations.literal: Formerly there were twenty-five hundred men from Yun as garrison troops, but with the Huang Chao rebellion communications were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: It once held a garrison of twenty-five hundred men from Yun Prefecture, but the Huang Chao uprising severed all contact with the interior.

sentences.zh: 超及城中漢戶百餘，皆戍兵之子孫也。

translations.literal: Chao and the more than a hundred Han households in the city were all descendants of the garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chao and the hundred-odd Han households still in the city were all descendants of that garrison.

sentences.zh: 其城今方幅數里，中有縣令、判官、都押衙、都知、兵馬使，衣服言語略如漢人。」

translations.literal: The city today measures several li on each side; within it are a county magistrate, an aide, a chief military adjutant, a chief clerk, and a horse-and-arms commissioner; dress and speech are much like those of Han people."
translations.idiomatic: The walled city now spans several li; inside are a county magistrate, aides, a chief military adjutant, clerks, and a horse-and-arms commissioner, and its people dress and speak much like Han Chinese."

sentences.zh: 即授超涼州刺史，充河西軍節度留後。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Chao as prefect of Liangzhou and made acting military governor of the Hexi Army.
translations.idiomatic: The court thereupon appointed Sun Chao prefect of Liangzhou and acting military governor of the Hexi Army.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，超卒，州人推其土人折逋嘉施權知留後，遣使來貢，即以嘉施代超為留後。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou, Chao died; the people of the prefecture chose the local man Zhebo Jiashi as acting military governor, sent envoys to present tribute, and Jiashi was appointed to replace Chao as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianyou era (948–950), Sun Chao died. The locals elevated the native leader Zhebo Jiashi as acting military governor and sent tribute to court; Jiashi was confirmed in Sun Chao's post.

sentences.zh: 涼州郭外數十里，尚有漢民陷沒者耕作，餘皆吐蕃。

translations.literal: Several tens of li beyond the walls of Liangzhou, Han people who had been cut off still farmed; the rest were all Tubo.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few dozen li of Liangzhou's walls, stranded Han farmers still worked the fields; beyond them lived only Tubo peoples.

sentences.zh: 其州帥稍失民情，則眾皆嘯聚。

translations.literal: If the prefectural commander slightly lost the people's favor, the masses would all gather in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the prefect lost popular support, the people would rise in armed assembly.

sentences.zh: 城內有七級木浮圖，其帥急登之，紿其眾曰：「爾若迫我，我即自焚於此矣。」

translations.literal: Within the city was a seven-story wooden pagoda; when the commander was pressed, he hastily climbed it and deceived the crowd, saying: "If you press me, I will burn myself here at once."
translations.idiomatic: The city held a seven-story wooden pagoda. When a commander was cornered, he would rush up it and warn the mob: "Press me further and I shall burn myself alive on this spot."

sentences.zh: 眾惜浮圖，乃盟而舍之。

translations.literal: The crowd cherished the pagoda, so they made a pact and let him go.
translations.idiomatic: The people, unwilling to lose the pagoda, swore an oath and released him.

sentences.zh: 周廣順三年，始以申帥厚為河西節度。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangshun of Zhou, Shen Shuaihou was first made military governor of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangshun (953), Zhou appointed Shen Shuaihou military governor of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 帥厚初至涼州，奏請授吐蕃首領折逋支等官，並從之。

translations.literal: When Shuaihou first arrived at Liangzhou, he memorialized requesting that the Tubo leaders Zhebo Zhi and others be granted offices, and all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Liangzhou, Shuaihou petitioned to confer official titles on Tubo chiefs including Zhebo Zhi; the court approved every nomination.

sentences.zh: 顯德中，師厚為其所迫，擅還朝，坐貶。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era, Shuaihou was pressed by them and returned to court on his own authority; he was demoted for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiande (954–955), pressure from the locals forced Shuaihou to abandon his post and return to court without leave; he was punished with demotion.

sentences.zh: 涼州亦不復命帥。

translations.literal: Liangzhou also no longer had a commander appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou thereafter received no further imperial commanders.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，靈武五部以橐駝良馬致貢，來離等八族酋長越嵬等護送入界，敕書獎諭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong, the five divisions of Lingwu presented tribute of fine camels and horses; the chiefs of eight tribes including Laili, Yuewei, and others escorted them to the border, and an imperial edict commended them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong (961), the five divisions of Lingwu sent fine Bactrian camels and horses as tribute; chiefs of eight tribes, including Laili and Yuewei, escorted the gifts to the frontier, and the emperor issued a commendatory edict.

sentences.zh: 秦州首領尚波於傷殺采造務卒，知州高防捕係其黨四十七人，以狀聞。

translations.literal: The Qinzhou leader Shang Boyu killed soldiers of the timber-gathering office; the prefect Gao Fang arrested forty-seven of his followers and reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Qinzhou chieftain Shang Boyu killed men of the timber-collection detachment; Prefect Gao Fang seized forty-seven of his followers and reported the incident.

sentences.zh: 上乃以吳廷祚為雄武軍節度代防安輯之，令廷祚齎敕書賜尚波於等曰：「朝廷製置邊防，撫寧部落，務令安集，豈有侵漁？

translations.literal: The emperor then made Wu Tingzuo military governor of Xiongwu Army to replace Fang and pacify the region, ordering Tingzuo to carry an edict bestowed on Shang Boyu and others, saying: "The court has arranged the frontier defenses and soothed the tribes, striving to keep them settled—how could there be encroachment and exploitation?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Wu Tingzuo military governor of the Xiongwu Army to replace Gao Fang and restore order, and sent him with an edict for Shang Boyu and his people: "The court has organized the frontier and sought to settle the tribes in peace. How could we tolerate encroachment upon them?

sentences.zh: 曩者秦州設置三砦，止以采取材木，供億京師，雖在蕃漢之交，不妨牧放之利。

translations.literal: Formerly Qinzhou established three stockades solely to gather timber and supply the capital; though they lay on the border between Fan and Han, they did not hinder the benefit of pasturage.
translations.idiomatic: The three stockades at Qinzhou were established only to harvest timber for the capital. Though they stand on the frontier between our peoples, they were never meant to interfere with your grazing rights.

sentences.zh: 汝等占據木植，傷殺軍人。

translations.literal: You seized the timber and killed soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you seized that timber by force and killed imperial soldiers.

sentences.zh: 近得高防奏汝等見已拘執，聽候進止。

translations.literal: Recently we received Gao Fang's memorial that you are already detained, awaiting further orders.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Fang has just reported that your leaders are in custody, awaiting my decision.

sentences.zh: 朕以汝等久輸忠順，必悔前非，特示懷柔，各從寬宥。

translations.literal: I consider that you have long rendered loyalty and submission and will surely repent your former wrongs; I specially show forbearance and grant each a broad pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Because you have long shown loyalty, I trust you will repent this offense. I therefore extend clemency and grant you all a full pardon.

sentences.zh: 已令吳廷祚往伸安撫及還舊地。

translations.literal: Wu Tingzuo has already been ordered to go and extend reassurance and restore your former lands.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tingzuo has been sent to reassure your people and restore your former territories.

sentences.zh: 所宜共體恩旨，各歸本族。」

translations.literal: You should together embrace the imperial grace and each return to your own tribe."
translations.idiomatic: Accept this grace in full and return each to your own tribe."

sentences.zh: 仍以錦袍銀帶賜之，尚波於等感悅。

translations.literal: Brocade robes and silver belts were also bestowed on them; Shang Boyu and the others were moved with gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade robes and silver belts were added to the gifts, and Shang Boyu and his people were deeply gratified.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，乃獻伏羌地。

translations.literal: That autumn they then presented the Fuqiang territory.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn they surrendered the Fuqiang region.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年，知西涼府折逋葛支上言：「有回鶻二百餘人、漢僧六十餘人自朔方路來，為部落劫略。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiande, Zhebo Gezhi, acting prefect of Western Liang, reported: "More than two hundred Uyghurs and more than sixty Han monks came by the Shuofang route and were plundered by tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qiande (966), Zhebo Gezhi, acting prefect of Western Liang, reported: "Over two hundred Uyghurs and more than sixty Han monks traveling the Shuofang route were robbed by local tribes.

sentences.zh: 僧雲欲往天竺取經，並送達甘州訖。」

translations.literal: The monks said they wished to go to India to fetch scriptures, and they were escorted all the way to Ganzhou."
translations.idiomatic: The monks said they were bound for India to obtain scriptures; we escorted them as far as Ganzhou."

sentences.zh: 詔褒答之。

translations.literal: An edict commended and replied to him.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued a commendatory reply.

sentences.zh: 五年，首領閭逋哥、督廷、督南、割野、麻裏六人來貢馬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the six leaders Lübuge, Duting, Dunan, Geye, and Mali came to present horses in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (967), six chiefs—Lübuge, Duting, Dunan, Geye, and Mali—presented horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 開寶六年，涼州令步奏官僧吝氈聲、逋勝拉蠲二人求通道於涇州以申朝貢，詔涇州令牙將至涼州慰撫之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaibao, the Liangzhou officials who presented memorials step by step, the monks Linzhansheng and Boshenglajuan, two men, sought a route through Jingzhou to present tribute to court; an edict ordered Jingzhou to send a military adjutant to Liangzhou to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaibao (973), two Liangzhou envoys, Linzhansheng and Boshenglajuan, petitioned for safe passage through Jingzhou so they could reach court with tribute; the emperor ordered Jingzhou to dispatch a military adjutant to Liangzhou to receive them.

sentences.zh: 八年，秦州大石、小石族寇土門，略居民，知州張炳擊走之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Large Stone and Small Stone tribes of Qinzhou raided Tumen, plundering residents; the prefect Zhang Bing drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (975), the Large Stone and Small Stone clans of Qinzhou raided Tumen and looted civilians until Prefect Zhang Bing repelled them.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，秦州安家族寇長山，巡檢使韋韜擊走之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, the Anjia tribe of Qinzhou raided Changshan; the patrol inspector Wei Tao drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo (977), the Anjia clan of Qinzhou raided Changshan; Patrol Inspector Wei Tao drove them back.

sentences.zh: 三年，秦州諸族數來寇略三陽、┒穰、弓門等砦，監軍巡檢使周承晉、任德明、耿仁恩等會兵擊敗之，斬首數十級，腰斬不用命卒九人於境上。

translations.literal: In the third year, various tribes of Qinzhou repeatedly came to raid and plunder the stockades of Sanyang, Jirang, Gongmen, and others; the military supervisors and patrol inspectors Zhou Chengjin, Ren Deming, Geng Ren'en, and others joined forces and defeated them, beheading several tens, and waist-cutting nine disobedient soldiers at the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (978), Qinzhou tribes repeatedly raided the stockades at Sanyang, Jirang, Gongmen, and elsewhere. Military supervisors and patrol inspectors Zhou Chengjin, Ren Deming, and Geng Ren'en combined their forces, killed dozens of raiders, and executed nine insubordinate soldiers by waist-cutting at the frontier.

sentences.zh: 太宗乃詔曰：「秦州內屬三族等頃慕華風，聿求內附，俾之安輯，咸遂底寧。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong then issued an edict, saying: "The three subject tribes of Qinzhou and others recently admired Chinese ways and hastened to seek inward submission; we made them settled and all attained peace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong then proclaimed: "The three subject tribes of Qinzhou and their neighbors lately turned toward Chinese civilization and sought to submit. We settled them in peace.

sentences.zh: 近聞乘蕃育之資，稔寇攘之志，敢忘大惠，來撓邊疆。

translations.literal: Recently we hear that relying on the strength of their breeding herds, they have ripened the will to raid and plunder, daring to forget great kindness and come to harass the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now, emboldened by their herds, they have taken to raiding again, forgetting our great kindness and harassing the border.

sentences.zh: 豈朕信之未孚，而吏撫之不至？

translations.literal: Could it be that my trust has not won their hearts, or that officials have not soothed them adequately?
translations.idiomatic: Has my trust failed to reach them, or have my officials fallen short in their care?

sentences.zh: 並蠲釁咎，特示威懷。

translations.literal: All border offenses are forgiven, and majesty and forbearance are specially displayed.
translations.idiomatic: I forgive all past offenses and again extend both firmness and mercy.

sentences.zh: 今後或更剽剠，吏即捕治，置之於法，不須以聞。」

translations.literal: Hereafter if they again plunder and slash, officials shall at once arrest and punish them according to law, without need to report upward."
translations.idiomatic: If they raid again, local officials may arrest and punish them by law without awaiting further orders from court."

sentences.zh: 是年，又寇八狼砦，巡檢劉崇讓擊敗之，梟其帥王泥豬首以徇。

translations.literal: That year they again raided Balang Stockade; Patrol Inspector Liu Chongrang defeated them and displayed the head of their chieftain Wang Nizhu as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: That same year they raided Balang Stockade; Patrol Inspector Liu Chongrang routed them and exposed the head of their chief Wang Nizhu as a warning.

sentences.zh: 三月，小遇族寇慶州，知州慕容德豐擊走之。

translations.literal: In the third month, the Xiaoyu tribe raided Qingzhou; the prefect Murong Defeng drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, the Xiaoyu clan raided Qingzhou; Prefect Murong Defeng repelled them.

sentences.zh: 八年，諸種以馬來獻，太宗召其酋長對於崇政殿，厚加慰撫，賜以束帛，因謂宰相曰：「吐蕃言語不通，衣服異制，朕常以禽獸畜之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, various peoples presented horses in tribute; Taizong summoned their chiefs to audience in the Chongzheng Hall, richly comforted them, and bestowed bolts of silk; he then said to his chief ministers: "The Tubo do not share our language and their dress is of another form; I have always kept them like birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (983), various tribes presented horses. Taizong received their chiefs in the Chongzheng Hall, treated them generously, and bestowed silk. He then told his chief ministers: "The Tubo speak another tongue and dress differently; I have always regarded them much as one would birds and beasts.

sentences.zh: 自唐室以來，頗為邊患。

translations.literal: Since the house of Tang they have been quite a frontier trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tang times they have been a persistent frontier menace.

sentences.zh: 以國家兵力雄盛，聊舉偏師，便可驅逐數千里外。

translations.literal: With the state's military strength mighty, if we merely raised a partial force we could drive them several thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: With our armies as strong as they are today, a single detached column could drive them a thousand li and more.

sentences.zh: 但念其種類蕃息，安土重遷，倘因攘除，必致殺戮，所以置於度外，存而勿論也。」

translations.literal: But considering that their kind breeds abundantly, is attached to its land and loath to move, if through expulsion slaughter would surely follow; therefore they are placed beyond concern, kept and not discussed."
translations.idiomatic: Yet they multiply on their own soil and are loath to leave it; any attempt to uproot them would mean slaughter on a vast scale. That is why I leave them beyond the pale of our concern—let them remain, and speak no more of it."

sentences.zh: 九年秋，秦州言蕃部以羊馬來獻，各已宴犒，欲用茶絹答其直。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year, Qinzhou reported that Fan tribes presented sheep and horses in tribute; each had already been feasted and rewarded, and they wished to use tea and silk to pay their value.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Qinzhou reported that frontier tribes had presented sheep and horses; the prefect had already feasted them and wished to pay them in tea and silk.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年，秦州大、小馬家族獻地內附。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunhua, the Large and Small Ma clans of Qinzhou presented territory and submitted inward.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chunhua (990), the Large and Small Ma clans of Qinzhou surrendered their lands and submitted.

sentences.zh: 二年，權知西涼州、左廂押蕃落副使折逋阿喻丹來貢。

translations.literal: In the second year, Zhebo Ayudan, acting prefect of Western Liangzhou and deputy commissioner for the left wing of Fan tribes, came to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (991), Zhebo Ayudan, acting prefect of Western Liangzhou and deputy commissioner of the left wing for Fan tribes, came to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 先是，殿直丁惟清往涼州市馬，惟清至而境大豐稔，因為其所留。

translations.literal: Earlier, the palace attendant Ding Weiqing went to Liangzhou to purchase horses; when Weiqing arrived the region was greatly fertile and ripe, and therefore he was detained by them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Palace Attendant Ding Weiqing had gone to Liangzhou to buy horses. The region was enjoying a bumper harvest, and the locals detained him.

sentences.zh: 靈州命蕃落軍使崔仁遇往迎惟清。

translations.literal: Lingzhou ordered the Fan-tribe army commissioner Cui Renyu to go and welcome Weiqing back.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhou dispatched Fan-tribe Army Commissioner Cui Renyu to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 又吐蕃賣馬還過靈州，為党項所略，表訴其事，因請留惟清至來年同入朝。

translations.literal: Also, Tubo selling horses on their return passed through Lingzhou and were plundered by the Tangut; they memorialized to report the matter and therefore requested that Weiqing be kept until the next year to enter court together.
translations.idiomatic: Tubo horse traders passing back through Lingzhou were robbed by the Tangut; they petitioned the court and asked that Ding Weiqing remain until the following year so they could enter court together.

sentences.zh: 詔答之。

translations.literal: An edict replied to them.
translations.idiomatic: The court assented.

sentences.zh: 四年，阿喻丹死，以其弟喻龍波為保順郎將代其任。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Ayudan died; his younger brother Yulongbo was made Langjiang of Baoshun to replace him in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (993), Ayudan died; his younger brother Yulongbo was appointed Langjiang of Baoshun to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 五年，折平族大首領、護遠州軍鑄督延巴率六穀諸族馬千餘匹來貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the great chief of the Zheping tribe, Supervisor Yanba of the Huyuanzhou army foundry, led more than a thousand horses of the Six Valleys tribes to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (994), Yanba, great chief of the Zheping clan and supervisor of the Huyuanzhou foundry, brought more than a thousand horses from the Six Valleys tribes as tribute.

sentences.zh: 既辭，復撾登聞鼓，言儀州八族首領逋波鵄等侵奪地土。

translations.literal: After taking leave, he again struck the Denunciation Drum at court, reporting that the eight-tribe chiefs of Yizhou including Tubo'e had encroached on and seized land.
translations.idiomatic: After his audience he struck the Denunciation Drum, charging that chiefs of Yizhou's eight tribes, including Tubo'e, had seized his people's lands.

sentences.zh: 上降敕書告諭之。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict of admonition.

sentences.zh: 知秦州溫仲舒上言，每歲伐木，多為蕃族攘奪，今已驅其部落於渭北。

translations.literal: The acting prefect of Qinzhou Wen Zhongshu reported that each year when timber was cut, it was largely seized by Fan tribes; he had now driven their tribes north of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Qinzhou Prefect Wen Zhongshu reported that each year's timber harvest was repeatedly seized by frontier tribes; he had now driven those tribes north of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 太宗慮生邊患，乃以知鳳翔薛惟吉對易其任，語見《惟吉傳》。

translations.literal: Taizong feared that border troubles would arise and therefore exchanged his post with Xue Weiji, prefect of Fengxiang; the account is in the Weiji biography.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing fresh border troubles, Taizong transferred him and appointed Xue Weiji of Fengxiang in his place, as related in Xue's biography.

sentences.zh: 是年春，知西涼府左廂押蕃落副使折逋喻龍波、振武軍都羅族大首領並來貢馬。

translations.literal: That spring, Zhebo Yulongbo, deputy commissioner of the left wing for Fan tribes at Western Liang, and the great chief of the Duoluo tribe of Zhenwu Army both came to present horses in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Zhebo Yulongbo, deputy commissioner of the Western Liang left wing, and the great chief of Zhenwu Army's Duoluo clan both presented horses at court.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，涼州蕃部當尊以良馬來貢，引對慰撫，加賜當尊虎皮一，歡呼致謝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao, the Liangzhou Fan leader Dangzun presented fine horses in tribute; he was led to audience and comforted, and Dangzun was additionally granted one tiger skin; he shouted with joy and gave thanks.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhidao (995), the Liangzhou chieftain Dangzun presented fine horses. Received in audience and richly rewarded, he was given a tiger pelt and shouted his thanks in delight.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，折平族首領握散上言，部落為李繼遷所侵，願會兵靈州以備討擊，賜幣以答之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year, the Zheping tribe chief Wosan reported that his tribe was being invaded by Li Jiqian and wished to join forces at Lingzhou to prepare for attack; gifts of silks were bestowed in reply.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year (996), Zheping chief Wosan reported that Li Jiqian was raiding his people and offered to rendezvous at Lingzhou for a joint campaign; the court rewarded him with silks.

sentences.zh: 七月，西涼府押蕃落副使折逋喻龍波上言，蕃部頻為繼遷侵略，乃與吐蕃都部署沒暇拽於會六穀蕃眾來朝，且獻名馬。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Zhebo Yulongbo, deputy commissioner for Fan tribes at Western Liang, reported that Fan tribes were frequently invaded by Jiqian; he then joined the Tubo frontier commander Moxiazhuaiyu in gathering the Six Valleys Fan masses to come to court, and also presented famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Yulongbo reported repeated Tangut raids and arrived at court with the Tubo frontier commander Moxiazhuaiyu and leaders of the Six Valleys tribes, presenting fine horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 上厚賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor richly rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded them generously.

sentences.zh: 是歲，涼州復來請帥，詔以丁惟清知州事，賜以牌印。

translations.literal: That year, Liangzhou again came requesting a commander; an edict made Ding Weiqing acting prefect and bestowed plaque and seal.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liangzhou again petitioned for an imperial commander; the court appointed Ding Weiqing acting prefect and granted him official plaque and seal.

sentences.zh: 咸平元年十一月，河西軍左廂副使、歸德將軍折逋遊龍缽來朝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Xianping, Zhebo Youlongbo, deputy of the left wing of the Hexi Army and General of Guide, came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the first year of Xianping (998), Zhebo Youlongbo, deputy of the Hexi Army's left wing and General of Guide, arrived at court.

sentences.zh: 遊龍缽四世受朝命為酋，雖貢方物，未嘗自行，今始至，獻馬二千餘匹。

translations.literal: Youlongbo's family for four generations had received court appointment as chiefs; though they presented local products, they had never come in person—now for the first time he arrived and presented more than two thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: For four generations his line had held imperial appointment as chiefs and sent tribute, but none had ever come in person. Youlongbo was the first to do so, bringing more than two thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 河西軍即古涼州，東至故原州千五百里，南至雪山、吐谷渾、蘭州界三百五十里，西至甘州同城界六百里，北至部落三百里。

translations.literal: The Hexi Army is the ancient Liangzhou: east to the former Yuanzhou one thousand five hundred li, south to Snow Mountains, Tuyuhun, and the Lanzhou border three hundred fifty li, west to the Ganzhou city border six hundred li, north to the tribes three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The Hexi Army is ancient Liangzhou: fifteen hundred li east to former Yuanzhou; three hundred fifty li south to the Snow Mountains, Tuyuhun, and the Lanzhou frontier; six hundred li west to Ganzhou; three hundred li north to the tribal lands.

sentences.zh: 周回平川二千里。

translations.literal: The circuit of level plain is two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: The surrounding plain extends two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 舊領姑臧、神烏、蕃禾、昌鬆、嘉麟五縣，戶二萬五千六百九十三，口十二萬八千一百九十三。

translations.literal: Formerly it governed the five counties of Guzang, Shenwu, Fanhe, Changsong, and Jialin, with 25,693 households and 128,193 persons.
translations.idiomatic: It once administered five counties—Guzang, Shenwu, Fanhe, Changsong, and Jialin—with 25,693 households and 128,193 persons.

sentences.zh: 今有漢民三百戶。

translations.literal: Today there are three hundred Han households.
translations.idiomatic: Today only three hundred Han households remain.

sentences.zh: 城周回十五里，如鳳形，相傳李軌舊治也。

translations.literal: The city circuit is fifteen li, shaped like a phoenix; tradition says it was the old seat of Li Gui.
translations.idiomatic: The walled city measures fifteen li around and is said to resemble a phoenix—the traditional seat, it is said, of Li Gui.

sentences.zh: 皆龍鉢自述云。

translations.literal: All this was Youlongbo's own account.
translations.idiomatic: All of this came from Youlongbo's own report.

sentences.zh: 詔以龍鉢為安遠大將軍。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Youlongbo Grand General of Pacifying the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed him Grand General of Pacifying the Distance.

sentences.zh: 二年，以儀州延蒙八部都首領渴哥領化州刺史，首領透逋等為懷化郎將。

translations.literal: In the second year, Kege, chief of all eight tribes of Yanmeng in Yizhou, was made prefect of Huazhou; the chiefs Toubo and others were made Langjiang of Huaihua.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (999), Kege, paramount chief of Yizhou's eight Yanmeng tribes, was appointed prefect of Huazhou, and chiefs including Toubo were made Langjiang of Huaihua.

sentences.zh: 四年，知鎮戎軍李繼和言，西涼府六穀都首領潘羅支願戮力討繼遷，請授以刺史，仍給廩祿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Li Jihe, acting commander of Zhenrong Army, reported that Panluozhi, paramount chief of the Six Valleys of Western Liang, wished to join forces to attack Jiqian and requested appointment as prefect with grain salary continued.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1001), Zhenrong commander Li Jihe reported that Panluozhi, paramount chief of Western Liang's Six Valleys, offered to join the campaign against Li Jiqian and asked to be made prefect with a state stipend.

sentences.zh: 經略使張齊賢又請封六穀王兼招討使。

translations.literal: The frontier commissioner Zhang Qixian also requested that he be enfeoffed as King of the Six Valleys and made Pacification Commissioner as well.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier Commissioner Zhang Qixian further proposed enfeoffing him as King of the Six Valleys and appointing him Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上以問宰相，皆曰：「羅支已為酋帥，授刺史太輕；

translations.literal: The emperor asked his chief ministers; all said: "Luozhi is already a tribal chieftain—making him prefect is too light;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted his chief ministers, who replied: "Panluozhi is already a tribal paramount chief—to make him a mere prefect is too slight an honor;

sentences.zh: 未領節制，加王爵非順；

translations.literal: he does not yet hold military command—adding a royal title would not be proper;
translations.idiomatic: he holds no military commission yet—conferring a royal title would be irregular;

sentences.zh: 招討使號不可假外夷。」

translations.literal: the title of Pacification Commissioner must not be lent to outer barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: and the title of Pacification Commissioner must not be granted to foreign peoples."

sentences.zh: 乃以為鹽州防禦使兼靈州西面都巡檢使。

translations.literal: He was therefore made Defense Commissioner of Yanzhou and concurrently Chief Frontier Inspector west of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore appointed Defense Commissioner of Yanzhou and Chief Frontier Inspector on the western approaches to Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時西涼使來，且言六穀分左右廂，左廂副使折逋遊龍缽實參羅支戎事。

translations.literal: At that time an envoy from Western Liang came and also reported that the Six Valleys were divided into left and right wings; the deputy of the left wing, Zhebo Youlongbo, actually shared in Luozhi's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A Western Liang envoy then reported that the Six Valleys were organized in left and right wings and that Youlongbo, deputy of the left wing, in fact shared Panluozhi's military command.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方務綏懷，又以龍缽領宥州刺史，六族首領褚下箕等三人為懷化將軍。

translations.literal: The court was then striving to soothe and embrace them; Youlongbo was also made prefect of Youzhou, and the three chiefs of six tribes including Chuxiaji were made Generals of Huaihua.
translations.idiomatic: As the court pursued a policy of conciliation, Youlongbo was also made prefect of Youzhou, and three chiefs of six tribes, including Chuxiaji, were appointed Generals of Huaihua.

sentences.zh: 其年，潘羅支遣部下李萬山率兵討賊，貽書繼和請師期。

translations.literal: That year Panluozhi sent his subordinate Li Wanshan to lead troops to attack the bandits and sent a letter to Jihe requesting a rendezvous for the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: That year Panluozhi dispatched Li Wanshan with troops against the Tangut and wrote to Li Jihe to arrange a joint operation.

sentences.zh: 先是，遣宋沆、梅詢等為安撫使、副，未行，上謂宰相曰：「 朕看《盟會圖》，頗記吐蕃反覆狼子野心之事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Song Hang and Mei Xun and others had been dispatched as Pacification Commissioner and deputy but had not yet set out; the emperor said to his chief ministers: "I have looked at the Alliance Chart and quite recall the Tubo's fickleness and wolfish, savage heart.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had appointed Song Hang and Mei Xun as Pacification Commissioner and deputy, though they had not yet departed. The emperor told his ministers: "I have been studying the Alliance Chart and am well reminded of how fickle and treacherous the Tubo have always been.

sentences.zh: 今已議王超等領甲馬援靈州，若難為追襲，即靈州便可製置，沆等不須遣，止走一使以會兵告之。」

translations.literal: It has now been decided that Wang Chao and others shall lead armored horses to aid Lingzhou; if pursuit is difficult, then Lingzhou can be arranged forthwith—Hang and the others need not be sent; only dispatch one envoy to inform them of the rendezvous for combined forces."
translations.idiomatic: We have already decided that Wang Chao and others shall lead troops to relieve Lingzhou. If pursuit proves difficult, Lingzhou can be secured without them—there is no need to send Hang and his party; dispatch a single envoy to arrange the joint campaign."

sentences.zh: 五年十月，羅支又言賊遷送鐵箭誘臣部族，已戮一人、縶一人，聽朝旨。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year, Luozhi again reported that the bandit Jiqian sent iron arrows to entice his tribes; he had executed one man and bound one, awaiting the court's decision.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fifth year (1002), Panluozhi reported that Li Jiqian had sent iron arrows to lure away his followers; he had executed one man and imprisoned another, and awaited the court's orders.

sentences.zh: 詔褒諭之，聽自處置。

translations.literal: An edict commended and instructed him, allowing him to dispose of the matter himself.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended him and authorized him to act as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 十一月，使來，貢馬五千匹。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, envoys came and presented five thousand horses in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month his envoys arrived with five thousand horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 詔厚給馬價，別賜彩百段、茶百斤。

translations.literal: An edict richly paid the price for the horses and separately bestowed a hundred bolts of colored silk and a hundred jin of tea.
translations.idiomatic: The court paid generously for the horses and additionally granted a hundred bolts of silk and a hundred jin of tea.

sentences.zh: 六年，又遣咩逋族蕃官成逋馳騎至鎮戎軍，請會兵討賊。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he again sent the Fan official Chengbo of the Miebo tribe, who rode swiftly to Zhenrong Army requesting combined forces to attack the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year (1003) he again sent the Miebo tribal officer Chengbo at full gallop to Zhenrong Army to request a joint campaign against the Tangut.

sentences.zh: 邊臣疑成逋詐，護送部署司，成逋懼，逸馬墜崖死。

translations.literal: Frontier officials suspected Chengbo of deception and escorted him to the deployment office; Chengbo, in fear, spurred his horse loose and fell from a cliff to his death.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials suspected treachery and escorted him under guard to headquarters. Terrified, Chengbo spurred his horse over a cliff and was killed.

sentences.zh: 上聞，甚歎息之，曰：「此泥埋之子，族人畏其勇，父子皆有戰功，凡再詣闕，朕皆召見，獎其向化。」

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this he sighed deeply and said: "This son of Nimai—his tribesmen feared his valor; father and son both had battle merit; twice he came to court and I summoned him each time, rewarding his turn toward civilization."
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this the emperor sighed deeply and said: "He was a son of the Nimai clan, feared by his people for his valor. Father and son had both won distinction in battle. He had come to court twice, and each time I received him and praised his turn toward civilization."

sentences.zh: 詔劾鎮戎官吏，仍令渭州以禮葬之。

translations.literal: An edict impeached the Zhenrong officials and ordered Weizhou to bury him with proper rites.
translations.idiomatic: He censured the Zhenrong officials and ordered Weizhou to bury Chengbo with full honors.

sentences.zh: 其年，原、渭蕃部三十二族納質來歸。

translations.literal: That year, thirty-two tribes of the Fan departments of Yuan and Wei sent hostages and came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: That year thirty-two Yuan and Wei frontier tribes sent hostages and submitted.

sentences.zh: 羅支又遣蕃官吳福聖臘來貢，表言感朝廷恩信，憤繼遷倔強，已集騎兵六萬，乞會王師收復靈州。

translations.literal: Luozhi again sent the Fan official Wu Fushengla in tribute; his memorial stated that he was moved by the court's grace and trust, resented Jiqian's stubborn defiance, had already gathered sixty thousand cavalry, and begged to join the imperial army in recovering Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Panluozhi again sent the tribal officer Wu Fushengla with tribute. In his memorial he declared himself grateful for the court's favor, furious at Li Jiqian's obstinacy, and ready with sixty thousand horsemen; he asked to join the imperial forces in retaking Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 乃以羅支為朔方軍節度、靈州西面都巡檢使，賜以鎧甲器幣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Luozhi was made military commissioner of the Shuofang Army and chief frontier inspector west of Lingzhou, and was granted armor and ceremonial goods.
translations.idiomatic: Panluozhi was appointed military commissioner of the Shuofang Army and chief frontier inspector west of Lingzhou, and received armor and ceremonial gifts.

sentences.zh: 又以吳福聖臘為安遠將軍，次首領兀佐等七人為懷化將軍。

translations.literal: Wu Fushengla was also made General of Pacifying the Distant, and seven subordinate chiefs including Wuzuo were made Generals of Cherishing Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fushengla was made General of Pacifying the Distant, and seven subordinate chiefs including Wuzuo were made Generals of Cherishing Transformation.

sentences.zh: 羅支屢請王師助擊賊，議者以西涼去渭州限河路遠，不可預約師期。

translations.literal: Luozhi repeatedly requested imperial troops to help attack the bandits; debaters held that Xiliang was far from Weizhou, separated by river and road, and that a rendezvous with the army could not be fixed in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Panluozhi repeatedly asked for imperial troops to join the campaign, but critics argued that Xiliang lay too far from Weizhou across river and road to fix a joint rendezvous in advance.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「繼遷常在地斤三山之東，每來寇邊，及官軍出，則已遁去。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Jiqian is usually east of the Dijin Three Mountains; whenever he raids the border and the official army goes out, he has already fled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Li Jiqian usually operates east of the Dijin Three Mountains. Whenever he raids the frontier and our troops march out, he is already gone.

sentences.zh: 使六穀部族近塞捍禦，與官軍合勢，亦國家之利。」

translations.literal: If the Liugu tribes are kept near the frontier to defend, and combine strength with the official army, that too is a benefit to the state."
translations.idiomatic: If the Liugu tribes hold the frontier and fight alongside our troops, that serves the state as well."

sentences.zh: 降詔許之。

translations.literal: An edict was issued approving this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 六月，知渭州曹瑋言隴山西延家族首領禿逋等納馬立誓，乞隨王師討賊，以漢法治蕃部，且稱其忠。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Cao Wei, prefect of Weizhou, reported that Tupu and other chiefs of the Yan clan west of Longshan had offered horses and sworn oaths, begging to follow the imperial army in punishing the bandits and to govern the Fan tribes by Han law, and praising their loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Cao Wei, prefect of Weizhou, reported that Tupu and other chiefs of the Yan clan west of Longshan had sworn allegiance with horse offerings, asked to join the imperial campaign, pledged to govern their tribes under Han law, and were commended for their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 詔授本族軍主。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him military chief of his tribe.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed him military chief of his tribe.

sentences.zh: 八月，者龍族首領來貢名馬，上嘉其嘗與潘羅支協力抗賊，令復優待之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, a chief of the Zhelong tribe came with famous horses in tribute; the emperor praised him for having once joined Pan Luozhi in resisting the bandits and ordered that he again be treated with favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month a Zhelong chief presented famous horses in tribute. The emperor praised his past cooperation with Panluozhi against the Tangut and ordered that he again receive favorable treatment.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，繼遷攻西蕃，遂入西涼府，知州丁惟清陷沒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year, Jiqian attacked the western Fan and then entered Xiliang Prefecture; the prefect Ding Weiqing was lost.
translations.idiomatic: That November Li Jiqian attacked the western tribes and took Xiliang Prefecture; Prefect Ding Weiqing was killed.

sentences.zh: 羅支偽降，未幾，集六穀諸豪及者龍族合擊繼遷。

translations.literal: Luozhi feigned surrender; before long he gathered the magnates of Liugu and the Zhelong tribe and jointly struck Jiqian.
translations.idiomatic: Panluozhi feigned submission, then soon rallied the Liugu magnates and the Zhelong tribe for a joint attack on Li Jiqian.

sentences.zh: 繼遷大敗，中流矢遁死。

translations.literal: Jiqian was utterly defeated, was struck by a flying arrow, and died in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiqian was routed, struck by a stray arrow, and died in flight.

sentences.zh: 者龍凡十三族，而六族附迷般囑及日逋吉羅丹。

translations.literal: The Zhelong numbered thirteen tribes in all, but six tribes followed Mibanshu and Ripojiluodan.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhelong comprised thirteen tribes in all; six of them followed Mibanshu and Ripojiluodan.

sentences.zh: 西涼府既聞羅支遇害，乃率龕穀、蘭州、宗哥、覓諾諸族攻者龍六族，六族悉竄山谷中，詔使者安集之。

translations.literal: When Xiliang Prefecture heard that Luozhi had been killed, it led the Kan'gu, Lanzhou, Zongge, and Minnuo tribes to attack the six Zhelong tribes; the six tribes all fled into the mountains and valleys, and an edict ordered envoys to pacify and settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Panluozhi's death, Xiliang Prefecture led the Kan'gu, Lanzhou, Zongge, and Minnuo tribes against the six Zhelong tribes, who all fled into the hills. The court sent envoys to pacify and resettle them.

sentences.zh: 六穀諸豪乃議立羅支弟廝鐸督為首領。

translations.literal: The magnates of Liugu then deliberated and set up Luozhi's younger brother Siduodu as chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Liugu magnates then chose Panluozhi's younger brother Siduodu as their leader.

sentences.zh: 且言鐸督剛決平恕，每會戎首，設觴豆飲食必先卑者，犯令雖至親不貸，數更戰討，威名甚著。

translations.literal: They also said that Siduodu was resolute, fair, and forgiving; whenever he met with Rong chiefs and set out cups and dishes for food and drink, he always served the lowly first; if orders were violated, even close kin were not spared; he had fought many campaigns, and his renown was very great.
translations.idiomatic: They praised Siduodu as firm yet fair: at gatherings of tribal chiefs he always served the humblest first; he showed no mercy even to kin who broke his orders; and his fame had grown through many campaigns.

sentences.zh: 詔授鐸督鹽州防禦使、靈州西面沿邊都大巡檢使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Siduodu Defender of Yanzhou and chief grand frontier inspector along the western border of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Siduodu was appointed Defender of Yanzhou and chief grand frontier inspector along the western border of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 上以遷黨未平，藉其腹背攻製，遂加鐸督朔方軍節度、押蕃落等使、西涼府六穀大首領。

translations.literal: Because Jiqian's faction was not yet pacified, the emperor relied on them to attack from front and rear and constrain them, and therefore further made Siduodu military commissioner of the Shuofang Army, commissioner for overseeing the Fan tribes, and great chief of the Six Valleys of Xiliang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Jiqian's followers still unrestful, the emperor sought to use Siduodu to pin them from both sides and therefore further appointed him military commissioner of the Shuofang Army, commissioner for overseeing the Fan tribes, and great chief of the Six Valleys of Xiliang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 涇原路言隴山縣王、狸、延三族歸順。

translations.literal: The Jingyuan Circuit reported that the Wang, Li, and Yan tribes of Longshan County had submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan Circuit reported that the Wang, Li, and Yan tribes of Longshan County had submitted.

sentences.zh: 又渭州言龕穀、懶家族首領尊氈磨壁餘龍及便囑等獻名馬，願率所部助討不附者；

translations.literal: Weizhou also reported that Zunzhanmobiyulong of the Kan'gu and Lan clans and Bianshu and others presented famous horses and wished to lead their followers to help attack those who would not submit;
translations.idiomatic: Weizhou also reported that Zunzhanmobiyulong of the Kan'gu and Lan clans and Bianshu and others presented fine horses and offered to lead their followers against those who refused submission;

sentences.zh: 又言西涼市馬道出本族，自今保無他虞。

translations.literal: it also reported that the Xiliang horse market route passed through their tribe, and from now on they guaranteed there would be no other cause for concern.
translations.idiomatic: and added that the Xiliang horse-trade route ran through their lands, which they pledged to keep secure hereafter.

sentences.zh: 詔賜馬直，以便囑等為郎將。

translations.literal: An edict paid the price for the horses and made Bianshu and others Lang generals.
translations.idiomatic: The court paid for the horses and made Bianshu and the others Lang generals.

sentences.zh: 石、隰州又言河西諸蕃四十五族內附。

translations.literal: Shi and Xizhou also reported that forty-five tribes of the western Fan along the Hexi had submitted inward.
translations.idiomatic: Shi and Xizhou also reported that forty-five Hexi frontier tribes had submitted.

sentences.zh: 其年，遷黨寇永寧，為藥令族合蘇擊敗之，斬首百餘級。

translations.literal: That year, Jiqian's faction raided Yongning and was defeated by Hesu of the Yaoling tribe, with more than a hundred heads taken.
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Jiqian's followers raided Yongning and were defeated by Hesu of the Yaoling tribe, with more than a hundred heads taken.

sentences.zh: 鎮戎軍上言，先叛去蕃官茄羅、兀贓、成王等三族及<者多>移軍主率屬歸順，請獻馬贖罪，特詔宥之。

translations.literal: Zhenrong Army reported that the three tribes of the former rebel Fan officials Qieluo, Wuzang, and Chengwang, together with the Enbo tribal military chief leading their followers, had submitted; they begged to present horses to atone for their crimes, and a special edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenrong Army reported that the three tribes of the former rebel officers Qieluo, Wuzang, and Chengwang, together with the Enbo tribal military chief and their followers, had returned, offered horses to atone for their crimes, and received a special pardon.

sentences.zh: 二年，廝鐸督遣其甥嗬昔來貢，仍上與趙德明戰鬥功狀；

translations.literal: In the second year, Siduodu sent his nephew Hexi in tribute and also submitted a report of battle merit against Zhao Deming;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Siduodu sent his nephew Hexi with tribute and submitted a report of victories against Zhao Deming;

sentences.zh: 又言蕃帳周斯那支有智勇，久參謀議，請授以六穀都巡檢使。

translations.literal: he also said that the Fan chieftain Zhousinazhi was wise and brave, had long joined in counsel, and asked that he be appointed chief frontier inspector of the Six Valleys.
translations.idiomatic: he also recommended the tribal chieftain Zhousinazhi as wise and brave, long active in counsel, and asked that he be made chief frontier inspector of the Six Valleys.

sentences.zh: 上嘉獎，從其請，仍賜茶彩。

translations.literal: The emperor commended and rewarded him, granted his request, and additionally bestowed tea and colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him, granted the request, and additionally bestowed tea and silk.

sentences.zh: 又追錄潘羅支子失吉為歸德將軍，厚賜器幣；

translations.literal: Pan Luozhi's son Shiji was also posthumously recorded as General of Returning Virtue and richly granted ceremonial goods;
translations.idiomatic: Panluozhi's son Shiji was posthumously made General of Returning Virtue and richly rewarded with ceremonial goods;

sentences.zh: 者龍七族首領有捍寇之勞，並月給千錢。

translations.literal: the chiefs of the seven Zhelong tribes who had merit in resisting bandits were all given a monthly stipend of a thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: and chiefs of the seven Zhelong tribes who had helped repel raids were each granted a monthly stipend of a thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 舊制，弓矢兵器不入外夷。

translations.literal: By old regulation, bows, arrows, and weapons were not sent to outer barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: By longstanding rule, bows, arrows, and weapons were not supplied to foreign tribes.

sentences.zh: 時西涼樣丹族上表求市弓矢，上以樣丹宣力西陲，委以捍蔽，特令渭州給賜。

translations.literal: At the time the Yangdan tribe of Xiliang memorialized requesting to purchase bows and arrows; the emperor, because Yangdan served on the western frontier and was entrusted with defense, specially ordered Weizhou to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangdan tribe of Xiliang then petitioned to buy bows and arrows. Because Yangdan served on the western frontier as a bulwark against invasion, the emperor specially ordered Weizhou to supply them.

sentences.zh: 因別賜廝鐸督，以重恩意。

translations.literal: Siduodu was separately bestowed upon as well, to deepen imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: Siduodu received a separate grant as well, to deepen the court's favor.

sentences.zh: 三年，又以者龍族合窮波、黨宗族業羅等為本族首領、檢校太子賓客，皆鐸督外姻也。

translations.literal: In the third year, Heqiongbo of the Zhelong tribe and Yeluoluo of the Dangzong clan were again made chiefs of their tribes and honorary guests of the crown prince; all were Siduodu's affinal kin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Heqiongbo of the Zhelong tribe and Yeluoluo of the Dangzong clan were again made tribal chiefs and honorary guests of the crown prince—all affinal kin of Siduodu.

sentences.zh: 鐸督遣安化郎將路黎奴來貢。

translations.literal: Siduodu sent the Anhua Lang general Lu Linu in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Siduodu sent the Anhua Lang general Lu Linu with tribute.

sentences.zh: 黎奴病於館，特遣尚醫視療。

translations.literal: Linu fell ill at the guest lodge, and an imperial physician was specially dispatched to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: Linu fell ill at the guest lodge, and an imperial physician was specially sent to treat him.

sentences.zh: 及卒，上憐之，厚加賵給。

translations.literal: When he died, the emperor pitied him and richly added funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the emperor took pity on him and granted generous funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 五月，鐸督又言部落疾疫。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Siduodu again reported epidemic sickness in the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Siduodu again reported epidemic sickness among his tribes.

sentences.zh: 詔賜白龍腦、犀角、硫黃、安息香、白紫石英等藥，凡七十六種。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed white dragon's brain, rhinoceros horn, sulfur, benzoin, white and purple quartz, and other medicines—seventy-six kinds in all.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted white dragon's brain, rhinoceros horn, sulfur, benzoin, white and purple quartz, and other medicines—seventy-six kinds in all.

sentences.zh: 使者感悅而去。

translations.literal: The envoy, moved and pleased, departed.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy departed deeply gratified.

sentences.zh: 又製加鐸督檢校太傅，其族帳李波逋等四十九人為檢校太子賓客，充本族首領。

translations.literal: An edict also advanced Siduodu to honorary grand tutor; forty-nine persons of his tribal household including Li Bobo were made honorary guests of the crown prince and installed as chiefs of their tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Siduodu was further made honorary grand tutor, and forty-nine members of his household including Li Bobo were made honorary guests of the crown prince and installed as tribal chiefs.

sentences.zh: 鐸督遣所部波機進賣馬，因言積官奉半歲，乞就京給賜市所須物，從之。

translations.literal: Siduodu sent his follower Boji to sell horses, and meanwhile reported that official stipends had accumulated for half a year; he begged to receive them in the capital and purchase what was needed, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Siduodu sent his follower Boji to sell horses and asked to collect half a year's accumulated stipends in the capital and buy needed goods; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 渭州言妙娥、延家、熟嵬等族率三千餘帳、萬七千餘口及羊馬數萬款塞內附。

translations.literal: Weizhou reported that the Miao'e, Yanjia, and Shurwei tribes led more than three thousand households, more than seventeen thousand persons, and tens of thousands of sheep and horses in coming to the frontier to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhou reported that the Miao'e, Yanjia, and Shurwei tribes had come to the frontier with more than three thousand households, over seventeen thousand people, and tens of thousands of sheep and horses to submit.

sentences.zh: 詔遣使撫勞之，賜以袍帶茶彩，仍以折平族首領撒逋渴為順州刺史，充本族都軍主。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched envoys to comfort and reward them, bestowing robes, belts, tea, and colored silk, and additionally made Saboke of the Zheping tribe Prefect of Shunzhou and chief military commander of his tribe.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent envoys to comfort them and granted robes, belts, tea, and silk; Saboke of the Zheping tribe was made Prefect of Shunzhou and chief military commander of his tribe.

sentences.zh: 是年，宗家、當宗、章迷族來貢，移逋、攃父族歸附。

translations.literal: That year, the Zongjia, Dangzong, and Zhangmi tribes came in tribute, and the Yibo and Safu tribes submitted.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Zongjia, Dangzong, and Zhangmi tribes sent tribute, and the Yibo and Safu tribes submitted.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔釋西面納質戎人。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, an edict released the Rong hostages held on the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict released the frontier hostages held on the western border.

sentences.zh: 先是，諸蕃有鈔劫為惡嘗經和斷者，恐異時復叛，故收其子弟為質，乃有禁錮終身者。

translations.literal: Previously, among the various Fan there were those who had plundered and done evil and had once been settled by peace agreements; fearing they might rebel again in the future, their sons and younger brothers were taken as hostages, and some were imprisoned for life.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, tribesmen who had raided and been bound by peace settlements had had their sons and brothers taken hostage for fear they might rebel again; some had been imprisoned for life.

sentences.zh: 上憫而縱之，族帳感恩，皆稽顙自誓不為邊患。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied them and released them; the tribal households were grateful and all bowed their foreheads to the ground, swearing themselves not to become a frontier trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity and freed them. Grateful, the tribes bowed to the ground and swore they would cause no further trouble on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 四年，邊臣言趙德明謀劫西涼，襲回鶻。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, frontier officials reported that Zhao Deming planned to seize Xiliang and raid the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year frontier officials reported that Zhao Deming planned to seize Xiliang and raid the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 上以六穀、甘州久推忠順，思撫寧之，乃遣使諭廝鐸督令援結回鶻為備，並賜鐸督茶藥、襲衣、金帶及部落物有差。

translations.literal: Because Liugu and Ganzhou had long been regarded as loyal and obedient, the emperor wished to soothe and settle them, and therefore dispatched envoys to instruct Siduodu to ally with the Uyghurs in defense, and also bestowed Siduodu tea, medicines, ceremonial robes, a gold belt, and tribal goods in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liugu and Ganzhou had long been loyal, the emperor sought to reassure them and sent envoys instructing Siduodu to ally with the Uyghurs in defense; Siduodu also received tea, medicines, ceremonial robes, a gold belt, and other gifts for his tribes.

sentences.zh: 鐸督奉表謝。

translations.literal: Siduodu submitted a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Siduodu submitted a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 三月，秦州曹瑋言熟戶郭廝敦、賞樣丹皆大族，樣丹輒作文法謀叛，廝敦密以告，約半月殺之，至是，果攜樣丹首來。

translations.literal: In the third month, Cao Wei of Qinzhou reported that the settled households Guo Sidun and Shangyangdan were both great clans; Yangdan repeatedly established wenfa and plotted rebellion, and Sidun secretly reported this, agreeing to kill him within about half a month; by this time he had indeed come carrying Yangdan's head.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Cao Wei of Qinzhou reported that the settled tribesmen Guo Sidun and Shangyangdan were both powerful clans. Yangdan had repeatedly organized rebellion under tribal law; Sidun secretly informed on him and agreed to kill him within a fortnight—and now arrived with Yangdan's head.

sentences.zh: 上以廝敦陰害樣丹，不欲明加恩獎，以疑懼諸族。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Sidun had secretly killed Yangdan, did not wish openly to add favor and reward, lest the various tribes be made suspicious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, unwilling openly to reward Sidun for secretly killing Yangdan, feared that doing so would alarm the other tribes.

sentences.zh: 時方議築南使城，遂以廝敦獻地為名，詔授順州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time the building of Nanshi City was under discussion, and so, under the pretext of Sidun's presenting land, an edict appointed him Prefect of Shunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Plans were then underway to build Nanshi City, so under the pretext of Sidun's land grant he was appointed Prefect of Shunzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，張佶深入蕃境，邊事數擾。

translations.literal: Previously, Zhang Jie had penetrated deep into Fan territory and frontier affairs were repeatedly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Zhang Jie had pushed deep into tribal territory and the frontier had been repeatedly unsettled.

sentences.zh: 及瑋破魚角蟬，戮賞樣丹二酋，由是前拒王師者伏匿避罪，瑋誘召之，許納罰首過。

translations.literal: When Wei defeated Yujiao Chan and executed the two chiefs Shang and Yangdan, those who had earlier resisted the imperial army hid themselves to avoid punishment; Wei summoned and enticed them, promising acceptance if they paid fines and surrendered heads for their offenses.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei defeated Yujiao Chan and executed the chiefs Shang and Yangdan, those who had earlier resisted imperial troops hid to escape punishment. Wei summoned them and promised amnesty if they paid fines and surrendered heads for their crimes.

sentences.zh: 既而至者數千人，凡納馬六十匹，給以匹彩。

translations.literal: Before long several thousand came; in all they presented sixty horses, and each was given a bolt of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: Soon several thousand came forward, presenting sixty horses in all; each received a bolt of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 或以少為訴者，瑋叱之曰：「是贖罪物，汝輩敢希利耶！」

translations.literal: Some who complained that it was too little were rebuked by Wei, who said: "These are things to redeem crimes—do you dare hope for profit!"
translations.idiomatic: When some complained the payment was too small, Wei rebuked them: "This is the price of atonement—do you dare haggle for profit!"

sentences.zh: 戎族聞之，皆畏服。

translations.literal: When the Rong tribes heard this, all feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes heard this and submitted in awe.

sentences.zh: 八月，曹瑋言伏羌砦廝雞波與宗哥族李磨論聚為文法，領兵趣之，悉潰散，夷其城帳。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Cao Wei reported that Sijibo of Fuxiang Stockade and Limolun of the Zongge tribe had gathered under wenfa; he led troops against them and they all scattered and fled; their stockades and tents were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Cao Wei reported that Sijibo of Fuxiang Stockade and Limolun of the Zongge tribe had organized under tribal law. He marched against them, they scattered, and their camps were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 九月，瑋又言宗哥唃廝囉、羌族馬波叱臘魚角蟬等率馬銜山、蘭州、龕谷、氈毛山、洮河、河州羌兵至伏羌砦三都谷，即率兵擊敗之，逐北二十里，斬馘千餘級，擒七人，獲馬牛、雜畜、衣服、器仗三萬三千計。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Wei again reported that Gusiluo of Zongge, Mabo Chila and Yujiao Chan of the Qiang tribes, and others led Qiang soldiers of Maxianshan, Lanzhou, Kan'gu, Zhanmaoshan, Tao River, and Hezhou to Fuxiang Stockade at Sandu Valley; he immediately led troops, defeated them, pursued them north twenty li, took more than a thousand heads, captured seven men, and obtained horses, cattle, miscellaneous livestock, clothing, and weapons numbering thirty-three thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wei again reported that Gusiluo of Zongge, the Qiang chieftains Mabo Chila and Yujiao Chan, and others had led Qiang forces from Maxianshan, Lanzhou, Kan'gu, Zhanmaoshan, the Tao River, and Hezhou to Fuxiang Stockade at Sandu Valley. He routed them, pursued them twenty li, took more than a thousand heads, captured seven men, and seized some thirty-three thousand horses, cattle, livestock, garments, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 吹麻城張族都首領張小哥以功授順州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaoge, chief of the Zhang clan of Chuima City, was appointed Prefect of Shunzhou for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaoge, chief of the Zhang clan of Chuima City, was made Prefect of Shunzhou for his service.

sentences.zh: 瑋又言永寧砦隴波、他廝麻二族召納質不從命，率兵擊之，斬首二百級。

translations.literal: Wei again reported that the Longbo and Tasima tribes of Yongning Stockade were summoned to send hostages but did not obey; he led troops against them and took two hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: Wei also reported that the Longbo and Tasima tribes of Yongning Stockade had refused summons to send hostages; he attacked them and took two hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 十一月，詔給秦州七砦熟戶首領、都軍主以下百四十六人告身。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, an edict granted commissions of office to one hundred forty-six persons below the settled-household chiefs and chief military commanders of the seven stockades of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month an edict granted commissions to one hundred forty-six settled-household chiefs and subordinate commanders of Qinzhou's seven stockades.

sentences.zh: 唃廝囉者，緒出讚普之後，本名欺南陵溫逋。

translations.literal: Gusiluo was descended from Zanpu; his original name was Qinanglun.
translations.idiomatic: Gusiluo traced his line to Zanpu; his original name was Qinanglun.

sentences.zh: 篯逋猶讚普也，羌語訛為篯逋。

translations.literal: Bianpu is still Zanpu; Qiang speech has corrupted it to Bianpu.
translations.idiomatic: Bianpu is simply Zanpu—the Qiang tongue had corrupted the name to Bianpu.

sentences.zh: 生高昌磨榆國，既十二歲，河州羌何郎業賢客高昌，見廝囉貌奇偉，挈以歸，置貢刂心城，而大姓聳昌廝均又以廝囉居移公城，欲於河州立文法。

translations.literal: Born in the kingdom of Gaochang Muyu, when he was twelve, He Langye, a Hezhou Qiang guest in Gaochang, saw that Gusiluo's appearance was remarkably imposing, took him back, and placed him in Gongxin City; the great clan Songchang Sijun also had Gusiluo live at Yigong City, intending to establish wenfa in Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the Gaochang kingdom of Muyu. At twelve, He Langye, a Hezhou Qiang visiting Gaochang, was struck by Gusiluo's imposing bearing, took him back, and settled him at Gongxin City. The great clan Songchang Sijun also installed Gusiluo at Yigong City, intending to establish tribal law in Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 河州人謂佛「唃」，謂兒子「廝囉」，自此名唃廝囉。

translations.literal: The people of Hezhou call the Buddha "Gu" and call a son "Siluo"; from this he was named Gusiluo.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hezhou tongue "Gu" meant Buddha and "Siluo" meant son; hence he was called Gusiluo.

sentences.zh: 於是宗哥僧李立遵、邈川大酋溫逋奇略取廝囉如廓州，尊立之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the monk Li Liyizun of Zongge and the great chief Wenbuqi of Miaochuan seized Gusiluo and took him to Huozhou, honoring and establishing him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Zongge monk Li Liyizun and the Miaochuan great chief Wenbuqi seized Gusiluo and brought him to Huozhou, where they raised him up as leader.

sentences.zh: 部族浸強，乃徙居宗哥城，立遵為論逋佐之。

translations.literal: As the tribes gradually grew strong, he moved to live at Zongge City; Liyizun was made lunbo to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: As his following grew stronger he moved to Zongge City and made Li Liyizun his chief minister.

sentences.zh: 立遵或曰李遵，或曰李立遵，又曰郢成藺逋叱。

translations.literal: Liyizun is also called Li Zun, also called Li Liyizun, and also called Yingchenglanbochi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liyizun is also called Li Zun, again Li Liyizun, and also Yingchenglanbochi.

sentences.zh: 論逋者，相也。

translations.literal: Lunbo means minister.
translations.idiomatic: Lunbo means "minister."

sentences.zh: 立遵念貪，且喜殺戮，國人不附，既與曹瑋戰三都穀不勝，又襲西涼為所敗。

translations.literal: Liyizun was greedy and fond of killing; the people of the state did not attach themselves to him; he had already fought Cao Wei at Sandu Valley without victory, and had also raided Xiliang and been defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liyizun was greedy and bloodthirsty, and his people would not follow him. He had already been defeated by Cao Wei at Sandu Valley and had also raided Xiliang and been beaten.

sentences.zh: 廝囉遂與立遵不協，更徙邈川，以溫逋奇為論逋，有勝兵六七萬，與趙德明抗，希望朝廷恩命。

translations.literal: Gusiluo then fell out with Liyizun, moved again to Miaochuan, and made Wenbuqi lunbo; he had sixty or seventy thousand victorious troops and resisted Zhao Deming, hoping for favor and appointment from the court.
translations.idiomatic: Gusiluo then broke with Li Liyizun, moved again to Miaochuan, and made Wenbuqi his minister. With sixty or seventy thousand seasoned troops he stood against Zhao Deming and looked to the court for favor and appointment.

sentences.zh: 知秦州張佶奏請拒絕。

translations.literal: Zhang Jie, prefect of Qinzhou, memorialized requesting refusal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jie, prefect of Qinzhou, memorialized urging rejection.

sentences.zh: 涇原鈐轄曹瑋上言，宜厚唃廝囉以扼德明。

translations.literal: Cao Wei, frontier commander of Jingyuan, submitted that Gusiluo should be treated generously to check Deming.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wei, frontier commander of Jingyuan, argued that Gusiluo should be treated generously to contain Zhao Deming.

sentences.zh: 而立遵屢表求讚普號，朝議以讚普戎王也，立遵居廝囉下，不應妄予，乃用廝鐸督恩例，授立遵保順軍節度使，賜襲衣、金帶、器幣、鞍馬、鎧甲等。

translations.literal: Yet Liyizun repeatedly memorialized requesting the title of Zanpu; court discussion held that Zanpu was king of the Rong, and Liyizun stood below Gusiluo and should not be rashly granted it; accordingly, following Siduodu's precedent of favor, Liyizun was appointed military commissioner of the Baoshun Army and granted ceremonial robes, a gold belt, ceremonial goods, saddle horses, armor, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liyizun repeatedly petitioned for the title of Zanpu, but court opinion held that Zanpu was the title of a tribal king and that Li Liyizun, ranking below Gusiluo, should not receive it rashly. Following Siduodu's precedent of favor, he was instead made military commissioner of the Baoshun Army and granted ceremonial robes, a gold belt, gifts, saddle horses, armor, and the like.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符八年，廝囉遺使來貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Gusiluo sent envoys in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1015), Gusiluo sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 詔賜錦袍、金帶、器幣、供帳什物、茶藥有差，凡中金七千兩，他物稱是。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed brocade robes, a gold belt, ceremonial goods, supplies and furnishings, tea and medicines in varying measure—seven thousand taels of gold in all, and other goods in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted brocade robes, a gold belt, ceremonial goods, supplies, tea, and medicines in varying measure—seven thousand taels of gold in all, with other gifts to match.

sentences.zh: 其年，廝囉立文法，聚眾數十萬，請討平夏以自效。

translations.literal: That year, Gusiluo established wenfa, gathered several hundred thousand men, and requested to campaign against Pingxia to prove his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: That year Gusiluo established tribal law, mustered several hundred thousand followers, and offered to campaign against Pingxia to prove his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 上以戎人多詐，或生他變，命周文質監涇原軍，曹瑋知秦州兼兩路沿邊安撫使以備之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the Rong were often deceitful and might otherwise produce other changes, ordered Zhou Wenzhi to supervise the Jingyuan army and Cao Wei to serve as prefect of Qinzhou and pacification commissioner along both frontier routes to guard against this.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the tribes' deceit and further trouble, the emperor ordered Zhou Wenzhi to supervise the Jingyuan army and made Cao Wei prefect of Qinzhou and pacification commissioner on both frontier routes to guard against it.

sentences.zh: 宗哥城東南至永寧九百一十五里，東北至西涼府五百里，西北至甘州五百里，東至蘭州三百里，南至河州四百一十五里。

translations.literal: From Zongge City southeast to Yongning is nine hundred fifteen li, northeast to Xiliang Prefecture five hundred li, northwest to Ganzhou five hundred li, east to Lanzhou three hundred li, and south to Hezhou four hundred fifteen li.
translations.idiomatic: From Zongge City it was nine hundred fifteen li southeast to Yongning, five hundred li northeast to Xiliang Prefecture, five hundred li northwest to Ganzhou, three hundred li east to Lanzhou, and four hundred fifteen li south to Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 又東至龕穀五百五十里，又西南至青海四百里，又東至新渭州千八百九十里。

translations.literal: East again to Kan'gu is five hundred fifty li; southwest again to Qinghai four hundred li; east again to New Weizhou one thousand eight hundred ninety li.
translations.idiomatic: Kan'gu lay another five hundred fifty li to the east; Qinghai four hundred li to the southwest; and New Weizhou one thousand eight hundred ninety li to the east.

sentences.zh: 九年，廝囉、立遵等獻馬五百八十二匹。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Gusiluo, Liyizun, and others presented five hundred eighty-two horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Gusiluo, Li Liyizun, and others presented five hundred eighty-two horses.

sentences.zh: 詔賜器幣總萬二千計以答之。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed ceremonial goods totaling twelve thousand in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The court replied with ceremonial goods totaling some twelve thousand pieces.

sentences.zh: 數使人至秦州求內屬。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent men to Qinzhou requesting to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly sent envoys to Qinzhou asking to submit to the court.

sentences.zh: 明道初，即授廝囉寧遠大將軍、愛州團練使，授逋奇歸化將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Mingdao reign, Gusiluo was immediately appointed Great General of Pacifying the Far and regimental commander of Ai Prefecture, and Wenbuqi was made General of Returning to Civilization.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Mingdao reign Gusiluo was made Great General of Pacifying the Far and regimental commander of Ai Prefecture, and Wenbuqi was made General of Returning to Civilization.

sentences.zh: 已而逋奇為亂，囚廝囉置阱中，出收不附己者，守阱人間出之。

translations.literal: Before long Wenbuqi rebelled, imprisoned Gusiluo and placed him in a pit, went out to gather those who would not follow him, and the pit guards secretly released him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wenbuqi rebelled, imprisoned Gusiluo in a pit, and went out to subdue dissenters; the guards secretly freed him.

sentences.zh: 廝囉集兵殺逋奇，徙居青唐。

translations.literal: Gusiluo gathered troops, killed Wenbuqi, and moved to live at Qingtang.
translations.idiomatic: Gusiluo rallied his troops, killed Wenbuqi, and moved his seat to Qingtang.

sentences.zh: 景祐中，以廝囉為保順軍節度觀察留後，歲以奉錢令秦州就賜。

translations.literal: During Jingyou, Gusiluo was made military commissioner and observation regent of the Baoshun Army; each year stipend money was sent for bestowal at Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyou era, Gusiluo was appointed military commissioner and observation regent of the Baoshun Army; each year his stipend was dispatched to Qinzhou for presentation.

sentences.zh: 元昊侵略其界，兵臨河湟，廝囉知眾寡不敵，壁鄯州不出，陰間元昊，頗得其虛實。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao invaded his borders and troops reached the Huangshui region; Gusiluo knew he was outnumbered, fortified Shazhou and did not emerge, secretly sent agents against Yuan Hao, and learned much of his strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao invaded his borders and brought troops to the Huangshui region, Gusiluo, knowing he was outmatched, shut himself up in Shazhou and sent covert agents against Yuan Hao, learning a great deal about his forces.

sentences.zh: 元昊已渡河，插幟誌其淺，廝囉潛使人移植深處以誤元昊。

translations.literal: After Yuan Hao had crossed the river, he planted banners to mark the shallows; Gusiluo secretly sent men to move them to deeper water to mislead Yuan Hao.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Hao crossed the river and planted banners to mark the fords, Gusiluo secretly had them moved to deeper water to deceive him.

sentences.zh: 及大戰，元昊潰而歸，士視幟渡，溺死十八九，所鹵獲甚眾。

translations.literal: When the great battle came, Yuan Hao was routed and retreated; soldiers followed the banners to cross, and eight or nine in ten drowned; the booty captured was very great.
translations.idiomatic: In the great battle Yuan Hao was routed; his men followed the banners to the ford and eight or nine in ten drowned. The booty Gusiluo took was immense.

sentences.zh: 自是，數以奇計破元昊，元昊遂不敢窺其境。

translations.literal: From then on he repeatedly defeated Yuan Hao with stratagems, and Yuan Hao no longer dared encroach on his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he repeatedly outmaneuvered Yuan Hao with stratagems, and Yuan Hao no longer dared probe his borders.

sentences.zh: 及元昊取西涼府，潘羅支舊部往往歸廝囉，又得回紇種人數萬。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao took Xiliang Prefecture, many of Pan Luozhi's old followers came over to Gusiluo, and he also gained several tens of thousands of Uyghur tribesmen.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao seized Xiliang Prefecture, many of Pan Luozhi's old followers defected to Gusiluo, and he also gained several tens of thousands of Uyghur tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 廝囉居鄯州，西有臨穀城通青海，高昌諸國商人皆趨鄯州貿賣，以故富強。

translations.literal: Gusiluo dwelt at Shazhou; to the west was Linggu City, which gave access to Qinghai; merchants from Gaochang and other states all flocked to Shazhou to trade, and by this means he grew rich and powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Gusiluo made his seat at Shazhou. Linggu City to the west opened the route to Qinghai, and merchants from Gaochang and other lands all converged on Shazhou to trade—by which means he grew rich and strong.

sentences.zh: 寶元元年，加保順軍節度使，仍兼邈川大首領。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoyuan, he was promoted to military commissioner of the Baoshun Army and retained the post of great chieftain of Miaochuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoyuan (1038), he was promoted to military commissioner of the Baoshun Army while retaining his title as great chieftain of Miaochuan.

sentences.zh: 時以元昊反，遣左侍禁魯經持詔諭廝囉，使背擊元昊以披其勢，賜帛二萬匹。

translations.literal: Because Yuan Hao had rebelled, Left Attendant Lu Jing was sent with an edict to instruct Gusiluo to strike Yuan Hao from the rear and break his strength; twenty thousand bolts of silk were granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao rebelled, the court sent Left Attendant Lu Jing with an edict urging Gusiluo to strike him from the rear and break his momentum, granting twenty thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 經還，以勞擢閣門祗候。

translations.literal: When Jing returned, for his labors he was promoted to gatekeeper attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, Lu Jing was promoted to gatekeeper attendant in recognition of his service.

sentences.zh: 廝囉奉詔出兵向西涼，西涼有備，廝囉知不可攻，捕殺遊邏數十人亟還，聲言圖再舉。

translations.literal: Gusiluo obeyed the edict and marched toward Xiliang; Xiliang was prepared, and Gusiluo knew it could not be taken; he captured and killed several dozen patrol scouts and quickly returned, declaring he planned another attack.
translations.idiomatic: Gusiluo obeyed the edict and marched on Xiliang, but finding it well defended and knowing it could not be taken, he killed several dozen scouts, withdrew at once, and announced he would attack again.

sentences.zh: 元昊既屢寇邊，仁宗召對魯經，欲再遣，經固辭，貶經為左班殿直。
