translations.literal: Since Yuan Hao had repeatedly raided the frontier, Emperor Renzong summoned Lu Jing for audience and wished to send him again; Jing firmly declined, and Jing was demoted to left-class palace direct.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Hao had repeatedly raided the frontier, Emperor Renzong summoned Lu Jing and wished to send him again; Jing firmly refused and was demoted to left-class palace direct.

sentences.zh: 募敢使者，屯田員外郎劉渙應詔。

translations.literal: The court recruited a daring envoy; External Affairs Officer of the Colonies Liu Huan answered the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The court sought a bold envoy, and External Affairs Officer of the Colonies Liu Huan answered the call.

sentences.zh: 渙至，斯囉迎導供帳甚厚，介騎士為先驅，引渙至庭。

translations.literal: When Huan arrived, Gusiluo welcomed and guided him with lavish provisions; armored horsemen served as outriders and led Huan to the hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Huan arrived, Gusiluo received him with lavish hospitality, sent armored horsemen ahead as escort, and led him to the hall.

sentences.zh: 廝囉冠紫羅氈冠，服金線花袍、黃金帶、絲履，平揖不拜，延坐勞問，稱「阿舅天子安否」。

translations.literal: Gusiluo wore a purple felt cap, a gold-thread brocade robe, a gold belt, and silk shoes; he gave a level salute without bowing, invited him to sit and inquired after his welfare, and said, "How fares Uncle the Son of Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Gusiluo wore a purple felt cap, a gold-thread brocade robe, a gold belt, and silk shoes. He gave a level salute without bowing, invited Liu Huan to sit, inquired after his welfare, and asked, "How fares Uncle the Son of Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 道舊事則數十二辰屬，曰兔年如此，馬年如此。

translations.literal: When speaking of old affairs he counted by the twelve zodiac animals, saying, "In the year of the Rabbit it was thus; in the year of the Horse it was thus."
translations.idiomatic: When recalling old times he reckoned by the twelve zodiac animals, saying, "In the year of the Rabbit it was thus; in the year of the Horse it was thus."

sentences.zh: 渙傳詔，已而廝囉召酋豪大犒，約盡力無負，然終不能有大功。

translations.literal: Huan delivered the edict; afterward Gusiluo summoned the tribal chiefs for a great feast and pledged to exert himself fully without failing them; yet in the end he could achieve no great success.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huan delivered the edict; Gusiluo then gathered the tribal chiefs for a great feast and pledged his full effort—but in the end achieved no great success.

sentences.zh: 後累加恩兼保順河西節度使、洮涼兩州刺史，又加階勳檢校官、功臣、食邑，賜器幣鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: Later he was repeatedly favored with additional titles—concurrently military commissioner of Baoshun and Hexi and prefect of Tao and Liang, also promoted in rank, merit titles, honorary office, fief, and granted vessels, silks, saddles, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was repeatedly honored with further titles—concurrently military commissioner of Baoshun and Hexi and prefect of both Tao and Liang—along with promotions in rank, merit titles, honorary offices, a fief, and gifts of vessels, silks, saddles, and horses.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐三年，摖羅部阿作等叛廝囉歸諒詐，諒祚乘此引兵攻掠境上，廝囉與戰敗之，獲酋豪六人，收橐駝戰馬頗眾，因降隴逋、公立、馬頗三大族。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiayou, Azuo and others of the Sheluo tribe rebelled against Gusiluo and submitted to Liangzha; Liangzha seized the opportunity to lead troops in raids on the borders; Gusiluo fought and defeated him, captured six tribal chiefs, seized many camels and war horses, and thereby subjugated the three great clans of Longzhou, Gongli, and Mapo.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiayou (1058), Azuo and others of the Sheluo tribe defected from Gusiluo to Liangzha, who seized the moment to raid the borders. Gusiluo defeated him, captured six chiefs, seized many camels and war horses, and thereby brought the Longzhou, Gongli, and Mapo clans to submission.

sentences.zh: 會契丹遣使送女妻其少子董氈，乃罷兵歸。

translations.literal: Then the Khitan sent envoys to deliver a woman as wife to his youngest son Dongzhan, and the armies were withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Khitan sent envoys to give a bride to his youngest son Dongzhan, and the armies were withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 治平二年夏，羌邈奔及阿叔溪心以隴、珠、阿諾三城叛諒祚歸廝囉，廝囉不禮，乃復歸諒祚，請兵還取所獻地，諒祚不之罪，為出萬餘騎隨邈奔、溪心往取，不能克，但取邈川歸丁家五百餘帳而還。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiping, summer, the Qiang Miaoben and his uncle Xixin rebelled against Liangzha with the three cities of Long, Zhu, and Anuo and submitted to Gusiluo; Gusiluo did not treat them well, so they returned to Liangzha, requested troops to recover the lands they had presented, and Liangzha did not punish them; he sent out more than ten thousand horsemen with Miaoben and Xixin to take them back; they could not succeed, but only recovered more than five hundred households of the Ding clan of Miaochuan and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second year of Zhiping (1065), the Qiang chieftains Miaoben and his uncle Xixin rebelled against Liangzha with the three cities of Long, Zhu, and Anuo and submitted to Gusiluo, who treated them coldly. They returned to Liangzha, asked for troops to recover the lands they had surrendered, and Liangzha did not punish them but sent out more than ten thousand horsemen with Miaoben and Xixin. They failed to retake the cities but brought back more than five hundred Ding-clan households of Miaochuan.

sentences.zh: 廝囉其年冬死，年六十九，第三子董氈嗣。

translations.literal: Gusiluo died that winter at the age of sixty-nine; his third son Dongzhan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Gusiluo died that winter at sixty-nine; his third son Dongzhan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 董氈母曰喬氏，廝囉三妻。

translations.literal: Dongzhan's mother was Lady Qiao, Gusiluo's third wife.
translations.idiomatic: Dongzhan's mother was Lady Qiao, Gusiluo's third consort.

sentences.zh: 喬氏有色，居曆精城，所部可六七萬人，號令明，人憚服之。

translations.literal: Lady Qiao was beautiful; she dwelt at Lijing City, and her following numbered some sixty or seventy thousand; her orders were clear and men feared and obeyed her.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Qiao was beautiful. She dwelt at Lijing City with some sixty or seventy thousand followers under her command; her orders were clear, and men feared and obeyed her.

sentences.zh: 方董氈少時，擇酋長子年與董氈相若者與之遊，衣服飲食如一，以此能附其眾。

translations.literal: While Dongzhan was still young, chiefs chose sons of chiefs of about the same age as Dongzhan to keep him company; clothes, food, and drink were all alike, and by this means he could win over his followers.
translations.idiomatic: While Dongzhan was still young, the chiefs chose sons of chiefs of about his age to keep him company, with identical clothes, food, and drink—by which means he won over his followers.

sentences.zh: 董氈自九歲廝囉為請於朝，命為會州刺史，而喬氏封太原郡君。

translations.literal: From the age of nine Gusiluo petitioned the court on Dongzhan's behalf, and Dongzhan was appointed prefect of Hui; Lady Qiao was enfeoffed as Lady of Taiyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: From the age of nine Gusiluo petitioned the court on Dongzhan's behalf; Dongzhan was appointed prefect of Hui and Lady Qiao was enfeoffed as Lady of Taiyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 其二妻皆李立遵女也，生瞎氈及磨氈角。

translations.literal: His other two wives were both daughters of Li Liyizun; they bore Xiazhan and Mozhanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: His other two wives were both daughters of Li Liyizun and bore Xiazhan and Mozhanjiao.

sentences.zh: 立遵死，李氏寵衰，斥為尼，置廓州，錮其子瞎氈。

translations.literal: When Liyizun died, Lady Li's favor waned; she was expelled and made a nun, placed at Huozhou, and her son Xiazhan was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Liyizun died, Lady Li fell from favor, was expelled and made a nun at Huozhou, and her son Xiazhan was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 磨氈角結母黨李巴全竊載其母奔宗哥，廝囉不能制，磨氈角因撫有其眾。

translations.literal: Mozhanjiao joined his mother's clan Li Baquan and secretly carried off his mother and fled to Zongge; Gusiluo could not restrain him, and Mozhanjiao thereby won control of his following.
translations.idiomatic: Mozhanjiao joined his mother's kinsman Li Baquan and secretly carried off his mother to Zongge. Gusiluo could not restrain him, and Mozhanjiao thereby won control of his followers.

sentences.zh: 李氏以寶元二年恩賜紫衣。

translations.literal: Lady Li was granted purple robes in the second year of Baoyuan as a favor.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li was granted purple robes as an imperial favor in the second year of Baoyuan.

sentences.zh: 磨氈角亦累奉貢，初補嚴州團練使，後以思州團練使卒。

translations.literal: Mozhanjiao also repeatedly sent tribute; he was first appointed regimental commander of Yan Prefecture and later died as regimental commander of Si Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mozhanjiao also sent tribute repeatedly; he was first appointed regimental commander of Yan Prefecture and later died holding that office at Si Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 所部立其子瞎撒欺丁，李氏懼孤弱不能守，乃獻皮帛、入庫廩文籍於廝囉，廝囉因受之。

translations.literal: His followers established his son Xiasaqiding; Lady Li feared she was too isolated and weak to hold out, so she presented hides and silks and surrendered the granary registers to Gusiluo, and Gusiluo accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: His followers installed his son Xiasaqiding. Fearing she was too weak to hold out alone, Lady Li presented hides and silks and surrendered the granary registers to Gusiluo, who accepted them.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐三年，命欺丁為順州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiayou, Xiqiding was appointed prefect of Shun.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiayou, Xiqiding was appointed prefect of Shun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 瞎氊居龕谷，屢通貢，授澄州團練使，先卒。

translations.literal: Xiazhan dwelt at Kanggu, repeatedly sent tribute, was appointed regimental commander of Cheng Prefecture, and died first.
translations.idiomatic: Xiazhan dwelt at Kanggu, sent tribute repeatedly, was appointed regimental commander of Cheng Prefecture, and died before the others.

sentences.zh: 子木征居河州，母弟瞎吳叱居銀川。

translations.literal: His son Muxizheng dwelt at Hezhou; his mother's younger brother Xiawuchi dwelt at Yinchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Muxizheng dwelt at Hezhou, and his mother's younger brother Xiawuchi at Yinchuan.

sentences.zh: 廝囉地既分，董氈最強，獨有河北之地，其國大抵吐蕃遺俗也。

translations.literal: After Gusiluo's lands were divided, Dongzhan was strongest, holding alone the lands north of the river; their state was in general Tubo custom.
translations.idiomatic: After Gusiluo's realm was divided, Dongzhan was the strongest, holding alone the lands north of the Yellow River; their polity largely preserved Tubo custom.

sentences.zh: 懷恩惠，重財貨，無正朔。

translations.literal: They cherished grace and favor and prized goods and wealth; they had no standard calendar.
translations.idiomatic: They cherished imperial favor, valued goods and wealth, and kept no official calendar.

sentences.zh: 市易用五穀、乳香、硇砂、罽毯、馬牛以代錢帛。

translations.literal: Market exchange used the five grains, frankincense, sal ammoniac, felt rugs, horses and cattle in place of money and silk.
translations.idiomatic: In trade they used grain, frankincense, sal ammoniac, felt rugs, horses, and cattle in place of coin and silk.

sentences.zh: 貴虎豹皮，用緣飾衣裘。

translations.literal: Tiger and leopard skins were prized and used to trim fur garments.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger and leopard skins were prized and used to trim fur coats.

sentences.zh: 婦人衣錦，服緋紫青綠。

translations.literal: Women wore brocade and dressed in crimson, purple, blue, and green.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore brocade in crimson, purple, blue, and green.

sentences.zh: 尊釋氏。

translations.literal: They honored the Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: They honored Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 不知醫藥，疾病召巫覡視之，焚柴聲鼓，謂之「逐鬼」。

translations.literal: They knew no medicine; when ill they summoned shamans to examine them, burned firewood and beat drums—called "driving off ghosts."
translations.idiomatic: They knew no medicine; when ill they summoned shamans, burned firewood, and beat drums in what they called "driving off ghosts."

sentences.zh: 信咒詛，或以決事，訟有疑，使詛之。

translations.literal: They trusted curses and sometimes used them to decide affairs; when lawsuits were doubtful, they made the parties curse each other.
translations.idiomatic: They trusted curses and sometimes used them to decide disputes; when a case was doubtful, the parties were made to curse one another.

sentences.zh: 訟者上辭牘，藉之以帛，事重則以錦。

translations.literal: Litigants submitted written petitions accompanied by silk; for weighty matters brocade was used.
translations.idiomatic: Litigants submitted written petitions with silk attached; for serious matters they used brocade.

sentences.zh: 亦有鞭笞杻械諸獄具。

translations.literal: There were also whipping, cangue, shackles, and other prison implements.
translations.idiomatic: They also had whips, cangues, shackles, and other instruments of punishment.

sentences.zh: 人喜啖生物，無蔬茹醯醬，獨知用鹽為滋味，而嗜酒及茶。

translations.literal: People liked to eat raw food; they had no vegetables, pickles, or sauces, knowing only salt for flavor, yet they were fond of wine and tea.
translations.idiomatic: People liked to eat raw meat; they ate no vegetables, pickles, or sauces, using only salt for flavor, yet they were fond of wine and tea.

sentences.zh: 居板屋，富姓以氈為幕，多並水為秋遷戲。

translations.literal: They lived in plank houses; wealthy families used felt for curtains; many gathered by water for autumn games.
translations.idiomatic: They lived in plank houses; wealthy families hung felt curtains, and many gathered by the water for autumn games.

sentences.zh: 貢獻謂之「般次」，自言不敢有貳則曰「心白向漢」云。

translations.literal: Tribute missions were called "banci"; when they said they dared not be disloyal they said "heart white toward Han."
translations.idiomatic: Tribute missions were called banci; when pledging loyalty they said, "My heart is white toward Han."

sentences.zh: 其後，河州、武勝軍諸族浸驕，閉于闐諸國朝貢道，擊奪般次。

translations.literal: Thereafter the tribes of Hezhou and the Wusheng Army grew increasingly arrogant, closed the tribute route of Khotan and other states, and attacked and seized tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the tribes of Hezhou and the Wusheng Army grew increasingly arrogant, blocked the tribute route from Khotan and other lands, and attacked and seized tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 詔邊將問罪。

translations.literal: An edict ordered frontier generals to demand an accounting.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered frontier generals to demand an accounting.

sentences.zh: 已而董氈遣使奉貢入謝，上慰納焉。

translations.literal: Before long Dongzhan sent envoys with tribute to enter and apologize; the emperor comforted and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Dongzhan sent envoys with tribute to apologize; the emperor accepted them with words of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 初，廝囉死，董氈嗣為保順軍節度使、檢校司空。

translations.literal: Initially, when Gusiluo died, Dongzhan succeeded as military commissioner of the Baoshun Army and honorary minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: When Gusiluo died, Dongzhan succeeded him as military commissioner of the Baoshun Army and honorary minister of works.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，加太保，進太傅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, he was promoted to Grand Guardian and then Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong ascended the throne, Dongzhan was promoted to Grand Guardian and then to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年，封其母安康郡太君，以其子藺逋比為錦州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xining, his mother was enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Ankang Commandery, and his son Linbubi was made prefect of Jin by parallel appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xining (1068), his mother was enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Ankang Commandery, and his son Linbubi was appointed prefect of Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年，夏人寇環慶，董氈乘虛入其境，大克獲。

translations.literal: In the third year, when the Xia people raided Huan and Qing, Dongzhan seized the opportunity to enter their territory and won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when the Tangut raided Huan and Qing, Dongzhan seized the opportunity to strike their territory and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 賜璽書袍帶獎激之。

translations.literal: He was granted an imperial letter, robes, and belt as reward and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: The court rewarded him with an imperial letter, robes, and belt.

sentences.zh: 王韶既定熙河，其首領青宜結鬼章寇河州踏白城，景思立死焉。

translations.literal: After Wang Shao had settled Xihe, the chieftain Qingyijie Guizhang raided Hezhou's Tabai City, and Jing Sili died there.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Shao had pacified Xihe, the chieftain Qingyijie Guizhang raided Tabai City in Hezhou, where Jing Sili was killed.

sentences.zh: 帝命邊臣招來之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered frontier officials to win them over.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered frontier officials to win them over.

sentences.zh: 十年，以鬼章及阿裏骨皆為刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, both Guizhang and Aligu were made prefects.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, both Guizhang and Aligu were appointed prefects.

sentences.zh: 董氈貢真珠、乳香、象牙、玉石、馬，賜以銀、彩、茶、服、緡錢，改西平節度使，遣供奉官郭英齎詔書、器幣至其國。

translations.literal: Dongzhan presented pearls, frankincense, ivory, jade, and horses; he was granted silver, brocades, tea, garments, and cash; his title was changed to military commissioner of Xiping; Palace Supply Officer Guo Ying was sent with an edict and ceremonial goods to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Dongzhan presented pearls, frankincense, ivory, jade, and horses and received silver, brocades, tea, garments, and cash in return. His title was changed to military commissioner of Xiping, and Palace Supply Officer Guo Ying was sent with an edict and ceremonial goods to his realm.

sentences.zh: 方鬼章犯境時，列帳訥兒溫及祿尊率部族叛附之。

translations.literal: When Guizhang was raiding the borders, the encamped chiefs Ne'erwen and Luzun led their tribes in rebellion to join him.
translations.idiomatic: While Guizhang was raiding the frontier, the encamped chiefs Ne'erwen and Luzun led their tribes in defection to his side.

sentences.zh: 既來降，又陰與董氈通。

translations.literal: After they had submitted, they secretly maintained contact with Dongzhan.
translations.idiomatic: After submitting, they secretly maintained contact with Dongzhan.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，詔知岷州種諤集酋長斬之，以妻女田產賜降將俞龍珂。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanfeng, an edict ordered Minzhou prefect Zhong E to assemble the chiefs and behead them; their wives, daughters, fields, and property were granted to the surrendering general Yu Longke.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yuanfeng reign, the court ordered Minzhou prefect Zhong E to assemble the chiefs and execute them; their wives, daughters, fields, and property were granted to the surrendering general Yu Longke.

sentences.zh: 二年，遣景青宜黨令支貢方物，以令支為珍州刺史，賜董氈錢萬緡，銀彩千計。

translations.literal: In the second year, envoys of the Jing Qingyi faction Danglingzhi presented local products; Danglingzhi was made prefect of Zhen; Dongzhan was granted ten thousand strings of cash and more than a thousand pieces of silver and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Danglingzhi of the Jing Qingyi faction presented local products; Danglingzhi was appointed prefect of Zhen, and Dongzhan was granted ten thousand strings of cash and more than a thousand pieces of silver and brocade.

sentences.zh: 三年，邈川城主溫訥支郢成及叔溪心、弟阿令京等款塞，以郢成為會州團練使，溪心內殿崇班，令京西頭供奉官，餘族人皆殿直奉職。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Miaochuan fort lord Wen'ezhiyingcheng and his uncle Xixin, younger brother Alingjing, and others opened the border in submission; Yingcheng was made regimental commander of Hui, Xixin inner palace attendant of the inner hall, Alingjing western head palace supply officer, and the rest of the clansmen were all palace direct and service attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, the Miaochuan fort lord Wen'ezhiyingcheng, his uncle Xixin, his younger brother Alingjing, and others submitted at the border. Yingcheng was made regimental commander of Hui, Xixin an inner hall attendant of the inner palace, Alingjing a western head palace supply officer, and the rest of the clansmen were all made palace direct and service attendants.

sentences.zh: 四年，王師討夏，會其兵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when the imperial army campaigned against Xia, his troops joined them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when the imperial army campaigned against Xia, his forces joined the campaign.

sentences.zh: 董氈遣酋長抹征等率三萬人赴黨龍耳江及隴、朱、珂諾，又集六部兵十二萬，約以八月分三路與官軍會。

translations.literal: Dongzhan sent the chiefs Mozheng and others leading thirty thousand men to Danglong'er River and Long, Zhu, and Kenuo, and also assembled one hundred twenty thousand from six divisions, agreeing to join the official army in three routes in the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: Dongzhan sent the chiefs Mozheng and others with thirty thousand men to Danglong'er River and to Long, Zhu, and Kenuo, and mustered a further one hundred twenty thousand from six divisions, agreeing to rendezvous with the imperial army in three columns in the eighth month.

sentences.zh: 帝以其協濟軍威，事功可紀，由常樂郡公進封武威郡王，鬼章、阿裏骨、黨令支皆團練使，心牟欽氈、阿星、李叱臘欽為刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he had aided military might and his merit was worth recording, promoted him from Duke of Changle Commandery to Duke of Wuwei; Guizhang, Aligu, and Danglingzhi were all made regimental commanders; Xinmuchin, Axing, and Lichilaxin were made prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had aided the imperial armies and his merit deserved record, the emperor promoted him from Duke of Changle Commandery to Duke of Wuwei; Guizhang, Aligu, and Danglingzhi were all made regimental commanders, and Xinmuchin, Axing, and Lichilaxin were made prefects.

sentences.zh: 夏人欲與之通好，許割賂斫龍以西地，雲如歸我，即官爵恩好一如所欲。

translations.literal: The Xia people wished to make peace with him, promising to cede lands west of Zhanlong and saying that if he returned to them, rank, titles, favor, and goodwill would be granted just as he wished.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangut sought peace with him, offering to cede lands west of Zhanlong and promising that if he returned to them, rank, titles, and favor would be granted just as he wished.

sentences.zh: 董氈拒絕之，訓整兵甲，以俟入討，且遣使來告。

translations.literal: Dongzhan refused, drilled and readied arms and armor to await marching in for punishment, and also sent envoys to report this.
translations.idiomatic: Dongzhan refused, drilled and readied his forces to await a punitive campaign, and sent envoys to report this to the court.

sentences.zh: 帝召見其使，使歸語董氈盡心守圉；

translations.literal: The emperor summoned his envoy and had him return to tell Dongzhan to guard the frontier with all his heart;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received his envoy and sent him back to tell Dongzhan to guard the frontier with all his heart;

sentences.zh: 每稱其上書情辭忠智，雖中國士大夫存心公家者不過如此。

translations.literal: each time he praised the loyalty and wisdom of his memorials, saying that even Chinese literati who kept the public interest at heart did no more than this.
translations.idiomatic: he repeatedly praised the loyalty and wisdom of Dongzhan's memorials, saying that even Chinese literati devoted to the public good did no more.

sentences.zh: 知邈川事力固不足與夏人抗，但欲解散其謀，使不與結和而已，故終不能大有功。

translations.literal: Knowing that Miaochuan's strength was not enough to stand against the Xia, he only wished to break up their designs so they would not ally—that was all—and so in the end he could achieve no great success.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Miaochuan's strength was insufficient to stand against the Tangut, he only wished to break up their designs and prevent an alliance—that was all—and so in the end achieved no great success.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong took the throne, he was promoted to honorary Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Dongzhan was promoted to honorary Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 元祐元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanyou, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanyou (1086), he died.

sentences.zh: 藺逋叱已死，養子阿裏骨嗣。

translations.literal: Lanbuchi was already dead; the adopted son Aligu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Lanbuchi was already dead; the adopted son Aligu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 阿裏骨，本于闐人。

translations.literal: Aligu was originally a man of Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: Aligu was originally from Khotan.

sentences.zh: 少從其母給事董氈，故養為子。

translations.literal: In youth he followed his mother in serving Dongzhan, and Dongzhan therefore adopted him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he followed his mother in serving Dongzhan, who therefore adopted him as a son.

sentences.zh: 元豐蘭州之戰最有功，自肅州團練使進防禦使。

translations.literal: In the Lanzhou campaign of Yuanfeng he achieved the greatest merit and was promoted from regimental commander of Su to defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the Lanzhou campaign of Yuanfeng he won the greatest merit and was promoted from regimental commander of Su Prefecture to defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 董氈病革，召諸酋領至青唐，謂曰：「吾一子已死，惟阿裏骨母嘗事我，我視之如子。

translations.literal: When Dongzhan was gravely ill, he summoned the tribal chiefs to Qingtang and said, "I have only one son, and he is already dead; only Aligu's mother once served me, and I regard him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: When Dongzhan was gravely ill, he summoned the tribal chiefs to Qingtang and said, "My only son is already dead; only Aligu's mother once served me, and I regard him as a son.

sentences.zh: 今將以種落付之，何如？」

translations.literal: Now I am about to entrust the tribe to him—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Now I mean to entrust the tribe to him—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 諸酋聽命。

translations.literal: The chiefs obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The chiefs assented.

sentences.zh: 既嗣事，遣使修貢。

translations.literal: After succeeding to office, he sent envoys to renew tribute.
translations.idiomatic: After succeeding to office, he sent envoys to renew tribute.

sentences.zh: 明年，裏骨奉表謝罪。

translations.literal: The next year, Ligou presented a memorial apologizing.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, Aligu presented a memorial of apology.

sentences.zh: 詔熙河無復出兵，許貢奉如故，加金紫光祿大夫、檢校太保。

translations.literal: An edict stated that Xihe would no longer send out troops, permitted tribute as before, and added Grand Preceptor of the Golden Purple Light and honorary Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that Xihe would send out no more troops, permitted tribute as before, and promoted him to Grand Preceptor of the Golden Purple Light and honorary Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 其廓州主魯尊欲焚拆河橋歸漢，熙州以聞。

translations.literal: His fort lord of Huozhou, Luzun, wished to burn and dismantle the river bridge and submit to Han; Xizhou reported this.
translations.idiomatic: His Huozhou fort lord Luzun wished to burn and dismantle the river bridge and submit to the Song; Xizhou reported this.

sentences.zh: 哲宗以裏骨既通貢，不可有納叛之名，欲弗納，又封其妻溪尊勇丹為安化郡君，子邦彪篯為鄯州防禦使，弟南納支為西州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhezong, because Ligou had already opened tribute relations, could not bear the name of harboring rebels and wished not to accept him; yet he also enfeoffed Ligou's wife Xizun Yongdan as Lady of Anhua Commandery, his son Bangbiaojian as defense commissioner of Shazhou, and his younger brother Nannazhi as prefect of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong, because Aligu had already opened tribute relations, could not accept Luzun without the stigma of harboring a defector; yet he also enfeoffed Aligu's wife Xizun Yongdan as Lady of Anhua Commandery, his son Bangbiaojian as defense commissioner of Shazhou, and his younger brother Nannazhi as prefect of Xi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 鬼章死，詔焚付其骨。

translations.literal: When Guizhang died, an edict ordered his bones burned and delivered.
translations.idiomatic: When Guizhang died, an edict ordered his bones burned and sent to the court.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年，以師子來獻。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng, a lion was presented in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaosheng (1094), a lion was presented in tribute.

sentences.zh: 帝慮非其土性，厚賜而還之。

translations.literal: The emperor feared it was not suited to the native climate, richly rewarded them and sent it back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, fearing it was ill suited to the climate, richly rewarded them and sent it back.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the third year, he died at the age of fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 瞎征嗣。

translations.literal: Xiazheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Xiazheng succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 瞎征，即邦彪篯也。

translations.literal: Xiazheng was Bangbiaojian.
translations.idiomatic: Xiazheng was Bangbiaojian.

sentences.zh: 以紹聖四年正月為河西軍節度使、檢校司空、寧塞郡公。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Shaosheng he was made military commissioner of the Hexi Army, honorary minister of works, and Duke of Ningsai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year of Shaosheng (1097), he was appointed military commissioner of the Hexi Army, honorary minister of works, and Duke of Ningsai.

sentences.zh: 性嗜殺，部曲睽貳。

translations.literal: By nature he was fond of killing; his followers were divided and estranged.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was bloodthirsty, and his followers were divided and estranged.

sentences.zh: 大酋心牟欽氈之屬有異志，忌瞎征季父蘇南黨征雄勇多智，共誣其謀逆，瞎征不能察而殺之，盡誅其黨，獨篯羅結逃奔溪巴溫。

translations.literal: Great chiefs such as Xinmuchin and others had different designs; they envied Xiazheng's younger uncle Sunan Dangzheng for his courage and wisdom, jointly accused him of plotting rebellion; Xiazheng could not discern the truth and killed him, executed all his faction, and only Bianluojie fled to Xibawen.
translations.idiomatic: Great chiefs such as Xinmuchin and his followers harbored other designs; envying Xiazheng's younger uncle Sunan Dangzheng for his courage and wisdom, they jointly accused him of plotting rebellion. Xiazheng failed to see through the charge and killed him, executed his entire faction, and only Bianluojie fled to Xibawen.

sentences.zh: 溪巴溫者，董氈疏族也，自阿裏骨之立，去依隴逋部，河南諸羌多歸之。

translations.literal: Xibawen was a distant kinsman of Dongzhan; since Aligu's enthronement he had gone to rely on the Longzhou tribe, and many Qiang south of the river came over to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xibawen was a distant kinsman of Dongzhan; since Aligu's accession he had gone to rely on the Longzhou tribe, and many Qiang south of the river rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 篯羅結奉溪巴溫長子杓拶據溪哥城。

translations.literal: Bianluojie supported Xibawen's eldest son Shaoza and seized Xige City.
translations.idiomatic: Bianluojie installed Xibawen's eldest son Shaoza and seized Xige City.

sentences.zh: 瞎征討殺杓拶，篯羅結奔河州，說王贍以取青唐之策。

translations.literal: Xiazheng attacked and killed Shaoza; Bianluojie fled to Hezhou and urged Wang Shan with a plan to take Qingtang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiazheng attacked and killed Shaoza; Bianluojie fled to Hezhou and urged Wang Shan with a plan to seize Qingtang.

sentences.zh: 已而溫入溪哥城，自稱王子。

translations.literal: Before long Wen entered Xige City and styled himself prince.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xibawen entered Xige City and styled himself prince.

sentences.zh: 元符二年七月，贍取邈川。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Yuanfu, Shan took Miaochuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year of Yuanfu (1099), Wang Shan seized Miaochuan.

sentences.zh: 八月，瞎征自青唐脫身來降。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Xiazheng escaped from Qingtang and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Xiazheng slipped out of Qingtang and submitted to the Song.

sentences.zh: 欽氈迎溪巴溫入青唐，立木征之子隴拶為主。

translations.literal: Qinzhuan welcomed Xibawen into Qingtang and installed Muxizheng's son Longzui as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhuan welcomed Xibawen into Qingtang and installed Muxizheng's son Longzui as chief.

sentences.zh: 九月，贍軍至青唐，隴拶出降。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Shan's army reached Qingtang and Longzui came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Wang Shan's army reached Qingtang, and Longzui came out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 以邈川為湟州，青唐為鄯州。

translations.literal: Miaochuan was made Huang Prefecture and Qingtang Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Miaochuan was made Huang Prefecture and Qingtang Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二酋雖降，然其種人本無歸漢意。

translations.literal: Although the two chiefs had surrendered, their tribesmen had no mind to submit to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Although the two chiefs had surrendered, their tribesmen had no wish to submit to the Song.

sentences.zh: 議者謂：「今不先修邈川以東城障而遽取青唐，非計也。

translations.literal: Commentators said: "If we do not first build fortifications east of Miaochuan but rush to take Qingtang, it is not a sound plan.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators argued: "If we do not first build fortifications east of Miaochuan but rush to seize Qingtang, the plan is unsound.

sentences.zh: 以今日觀之，有不可守者四：自炳靈寺渡河至青唐四百里，道險地遠，緩急聲援不相及，一也；

translations.literal: Viewed as of today, there are four reasons it cannot be held: from Bingling Temple, crossing the river to Qingtang is four hundred li—the road is perilous and the land remote, so in crisis reinforcements cannot reach in time—this is the first;
translations.idiomatic: Viewed from the present situation, there are four reasons it cannot be held: from Bingling Temple, crossing the river to Qingtang is four hundred li—the road is perilous and the land remote, so in an emergency reinforcements cannot arrive in time—this is the first;

sentences.zh: 羌若斷橋塞隘，我雖有百萬之師，倉卒不能進，二也；

translations.literal: If the Qiang destroy bridges and block passes, even though we have an army of a million, we cannot advance in haste—this is the second;
translations.idiomatic: If the Qiang destroy bridges and block the passes, even an army of a million could not advance in haste—this is the second;

sentences.zh: 王贍提孤軍以入，四無援兵，必生他變，三也；

translations.literal: Wang Shan led an isolated army inward with no reinforcements on any of four sides—other troubles would surely arise—this is the third;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shan led an isolated army inward with no reinforcements on any side—other troubles would surely arise—this is the third;

sentences.zh: 設遣大軍而青唐、宗哥、邈川食皆止支一月，內地無糧可運，難以久處，四也。

translations.literal: Even if a large army were sent, provisions at Qingtang, Zongge, and Miaochuan would only last one month, and with no grain transportable from the interior, troops could not remain long—this is the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Even if a large army were sent, provisions at Qingtang, Zongge, and Miaochuan would last only one month, and with no grain transportable from the interior, troops could not remain there long—this is the fourth.

sentences.zh: 官軍自會州還者皆憔悴，衣屨穿決，器仗不全，羌視之有輕漢心，旦夕必叛。」

translations.literal: The government troops returning from Huizhou were all haggard, their clothes and shoes torn, their weapons incomplete; the Qiang looked on them with contempt for Han, and rebellion was inevitable before long."
translations.idiomatic: The government troops returning from Huizhou were haggard, their clothes and shoes in tatters, their weapons incomplete; the Qiang looked on them with contempt for the Han, and rebellion was inevitable before long."

sentences.zh: 閏九月，欽氈等果與青唐城中人相結，謀復奪城。

translations.literal: In the intercalary ninth month, Qinzhuan and others indeed joined with people inside Qingtang city in a plot to retake the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary ninth month, Qinzhuan and his followers indeed conspired with people inside Qingtang to retake the city.

sentences.zh: 山南諸羌亦叛。

translations.literal: The Qiang south of the mountains also rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang south of the mountains also rebelled.

sentences.zh: 贍遣將破之，戮結咓齪及欽氈等九人。

translations.literal: Shan sent generals to defeat them and executed Jieluocuo and Qinzhuan among nine men.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shan sent generals to defeat them and executed Jieluocuo, Qinzhuan, and seven others.

sentences.zh: 青唐圍解而邈川益急，夏人十萬助之。

translations.literal: The siege of Qingtang was lifted, but Miaochuan grew more desperate; a hundred thousand Xia troops came to aid them.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Qingtang was lifted, but the pressure on Miaochuan grew worse as a hundred thousand Tangut troops came to their aid.

sentences.zh: 總管王湣以死戰固守，乃得免。

translations.literal: Chief commandant Wang Min held firm through desperate fighting and only then escaped destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Chief commandant Wang Min held on through desperate fighting and only then escaped destruction.

sentences.zh: 贍棄青唐歸，巴溫與其子溪賒羅撒據之。

translations.literal: Shan abandoned Qingtang and withdrew; Bawen and his son Xishaluosa seized it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shan abandoned Qingtang and withdrew; Xibawen and his son Xishaluosa seized it.

sentences.zh: 朝論請並棄邈川，且謂董氈無後，隴拶乃木征之子、唃廝囉嫡曾孫，最為親的。

translations.literal: Court opinion urged abandoning Miaochuan as well, and held that Dongzhan had no heir; Longzui was the son of Muxizheng and Gusiluo's legitimate great-grandson—the closest kin.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion urged abandoning Miaochuan as well, arguing that Dongzhan had no heir and that Longzui, as the son of Muxizheng and Gusiluo's legitimate great-grandson, was the closest in the line of succession.

sentences.zh: 於是以隴拶為河西軍節度使、知鄯州，封武威郡公，充西蕃都護，依府州折氏世世承襲。

translations.literal: Thereupon Longzui was made military commissioner of the Hexi Army and prefect of Shan, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuwei, appointed protector-general of the Western Tribes, with hereditary succession on the model of the Zhe clan of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Longzui was appointed military commissioner of the Hexi Army and prefect of Shan, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuwei, and made protector-general of the Western Tribes, with hereditary succession on the model of the Zhe clan of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋賜姓名曰趙懷德；

translations.literal: Soon he was granted the surname and personal name Zhao Huai De;
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was granted the surname and personal name Zhao Huai De;

sentences.zh: 其弟邦辟勿丁咓曰懷義，為廓州團練使、同知湟州；

translations.literal: his younger brother Bangbiwudinglao was named Huaiyi, made regimental commander of Huo and concurrently prefect of Huang;
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother Bangbiwudinglao was named Huaiyi and appointed regimental commander of Huo and concurrently prefect of Huang;

sentences.zh: 加瞎征檢校太傅、懷遠軍節度使。

translations.literal: Xiazheng was additionally made honorary grand preceptor and military commissioner of Huaiyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Xiazheng was additionally made honorary grand preceptor and military commissioner of Huaiyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，懷德及所降契丹、夏國、回鶻公主入見，各賜冠服，退易之，於邇英閣前後立班謝，賜食於橫門。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year, Huai De and the princesses surrendered from Khitan, Xia, and Uyghur realms had audience; each was granted cap and robes, changed out of them, stood in ranks before and after Yingying Pavilion to give thanks, and were given food at Heng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year, Huai De and the princesses who had submitted from Khitan, Tangut, and Uyghur realms had audience at court. Each was granted cap and robes, changed out of them, stood in ranks before and after Yingying Pavilion to give thanks, and was given a meal at Heng Gate.

sentences.zh: 徽宗命輔臣呼與語，問何以招致溪巴溫，對曰：「譬如乳牛，係其子即母須來，係其母即子須來。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong ordered his ministers to summon them for conversation and asked how Xibawen might be won over; he replied: "It is like a milk cow—tie up the calf and the mother must come; tie up the mother and the calf must come.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong ordered his ministers to summon them and asked how Xibawen might be won over. Huai De replied: "It is like a milk cow—tie up the calf and the mother must come; tie up the mother and the calf must come.

sentences.zh: 俟至岷州，當遣人往諭，使之歸漢。」

translations.literal: When we reach Min Prefecture, I shall send someone to instruct him and bring him to submit to Han."
translations.idiomatic: When we reach Min Prefecture, I shall send someone to instruct him and bring him to submit to the Song."

sentences.zh: 遂與瞎征俱還湟州。

translations.literal: He then returned to Huang Prefecture together with Xiazheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to Huang Prefecture together with Xiazheng.

sentences.zh: 溪賒羅撒謀襲殺懷德，懷德奔河南。

translations.literal: Xishaluosa plotted to ambush and kill Huai De; Huai De fled south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Xishaluosa plotted to ambush and kill Huai De, who fled south of the river.

sentences.zh: 瞎征不自安，求內徙，詔居鄧州。

translations.literal: Xiazheng felt insecure, requested relocation inward, and an edict assigned him to Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiazheng felt insecure and requested relocation to the interior; an edict assigned him to Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 崇寧元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongning, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongning (1102), he died.

sentences.zh: 三年，王厚復湟、鄯。

translations.literal: In the third year, Wang Hou recovered Huang and Shan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Wang Hou recovered Huang and Shan.

sentences.zh: 懷德至京師，拜感德軍節度使，封安化郡王。

translations.literal: Huai De came to the capital, was appointed military commissioner of Gande Army, and enfeoffed as Prince of Anhua Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Huai De came to the capital, was appointed military commissioner of Gande Army, and enfeoffed as Prince of Anhua Commandery.

sentences.zh: 趙思忠即瞎氈之子木征也。

translations.literal: Zhao Sizhong was Xiazhan's son Muxizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Sizhong was Xiazhan's son Muxizheng.

sentences.zh: 瞎氈死，木征不能自立，青唐族酋瞎藥雞囉及僧鹿遵迎之居洮州，欲立以服洮岷疊宕、武勝軍諸羌。

translations.literal: When Xiazhan died, Muxizheng could not stand on his own; Qingtang tribal chiefs Xiayaojiluo and the monk Sengluzun welcomed him to dwell at Tao Prefecture, intending to install him to bring the Qiang of Tao, Min, Die, Dang, and Wusheng Army to submission.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiazhan died, Muxizheng could not stand on his own. Qingtang tribal chiefs Xiayaojiluo and the monk Sengluzun welcomed him to Tao Prefecture, intending to install him so as to bring the Qiang of Tao, Min, Die, Dang, and Wusheng Army to submission.

sentences.zh: 秦州以其近邊，逐之，乃還河州，後徙安江城，董氈欲羈屬之，不能有也。

translations.literal: Qin Prefecture, because he was near the border, drove him out; he returned to He Prefecture, later moved to Anjiang City; Dongzhan wished to hold him in subordination but could not.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Prefecture, because he was too close to the border, drove him out. He returned to He Prefecture and later moved to Anjiang City. Dongzhan wished to keep him under constraint but could not.

sentences.zh: 母弟瞎吳叱，別居銀川聶家山，至和初，補本族副軍主。

translations.literal: His younger brother by the same mother, Xiawuchi, lived separately at Nie Family Mountain in Yinchuan; at the beginning of Zhihe he was appointed deputy chieftain of the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother by the same mother, Xiawuchi, lived separately at Nie Family Mountain in Yinchuan; at the beginning of Zhihe (1054), he was appointed deputy chieftain of the tribe.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，為河州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Jiayou era he was made prefect of He.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiayou era (1056–1063), he was made prefect of He.

sentences.zh: 王韶經略熙河，遣僧智緣往說之，啖以厚利，因隨以兵；

translations.literal: Wang Shao as frontier commissioner of Xihe sent the monk Zhiyuan to persuade him, tempted him with rich rewards, and therefore followed with troops;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao, as frontier commissioner of Xihe, sent the monk Zhiyuan to persuade him, tempted him with rich rewards, and then followed with troops;

sentences.zh: 前後殺其老弱數千，焚族帳萬數，得腹心酋領十餘人，又禽其妻子，皆不殺。

translations.literal: In succession they killed several thousand of his elderly and weak, burned tens of thousands of tents, captured more than ten trusted chieftains, and also seized their wives and children—all without killing them.
translations.idiomatic: In succession they killed several thousand of his elderly and weak, burned tens of thousands of tents, captured more than ten trusted chieftains, and also seized their wives and children—all without killing them.

sentences.zh: 遂以熙寧七年四月舉洮、河二州來降，賜以姓名，拜榮州團練使。

translations.literal: Thereupon in the fourth month of the seventh year of Xining he brought Tao and He prefectures to surrender; he was granted a surname and personal name and appointed regimental commander of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon in the fourth month of the seventh year of Xining (1074), he brought Tao and He prefectures to surrender, was granted the surname and personal name Zhao Sizhong, and was appointed regimental commander of Rong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 封其母郢成結遂寧郡太夫人，妻包氏咸寧郡君。

translations.literal: His mother Yingchengjie was enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Suining Commandery; his wife Lady Bao as Lady of Xianning Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Yingchengjie was enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Suining Commandery, and his wife Lady Bao as Lady of Xianning Commandery.

sentences.zh: 弟董穀賜名繼忠，補六宅副使。

translations.literal: His younger brother Donggu was given the name Jizhong and appointed deputy commissioner of the Six Residences.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Donggu was given the name Jizhong and appointed deputy commissioner of the Six Residences.

sentences.zh: 結吳延征賜名濟忠，瞎吳叱曰紹忠，巴氈角曰醇忠，巴氈抹曰存忠；

translations.literal: Jiewuyanzheng was named Jizhong, Xiawuchi Shaozhong, Bazhanjiao Chunzhong, and Bazhanmo Cunzhong;
translations.idiomatic: Jiewuyanzheng was named Jizhong, Xiawuchi Shaozhong, Bazhanjiao Chunzhong, and Bazhanmo Cunzhong;

sentences.zh: 長子邦辟勿丁咓曰懷義，次蓋咓日秉義，皆超拜官。

translations.literal: The eldest son Bangbiwudinglao was named Huaiyi, the second Gairuori Bingyi—all were promoted to office above their station.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Bangbiwudinglao was named Huaiyi, the second Gairuori Bingyi—all were promoted to office above their station.

sentences.zh: 以思忠為秦州鈐轄，不涖事，而乞主熙河羌部，經略司以為不可。

translations.literal: Sizhong was made frontier commander of Qin but did not personally attend to duties; he petitioned to oversee the Qiang tribes of Xihe, but the frontier commission deemed it inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong was made frontier commander of Qin but did not personally attend to duties; he petitioned to oversee the Qiang tribes of Xihe, but the frontier commission deemed it inadvisable.

sentences.zh: 詔以二州給地五十頃。

translations.literal: An edict granted fifty qing of land from the two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted fifty qing of land from the two prefectures.

sentences.zh: 後遷合州防禦使，卒，贈鎮洮軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to defender of He Prefecture; when he died he was posthumously awarded military commissioner and observation intendant of Zhentao Army.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to defender of He Prefecture; when he died he was posthumously awarded military commissioner and observation intendant of Zhentao Army.
